title: bug: chat_completion_files_handler runs legacy RAG pipeline alongside native function calling for uploaded files with Focused Retrieval
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues.
- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions.
- [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items.
- [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI.

### Installation Method

Docker

### Open WebUI Version

v0.8.12 (also reproducible on current `main`)

### Ollama Version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Operating System

Linux

### Browser (if applicable)

Chrome / Firefox

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.
- [x] I have included the Docker container logs.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.**
- [x] I have clearly **listed every relevant configuration, custom setting, environment variable, and command-line option that influences my setup.**
- [x] I have documented **step-by-step reproduction instructions that are precise, sequential, and leave nothing to interpretation**.

### Expected Behavior

When a model has **native function calling** enabled and a user uploads a file to the chat, the legacy RAG pipeline (task-model query generation → embedding → vector search → RAG template injection) should **not** run - regardless of whether the file is set to "Using Focused Retrieval" or "Use Entire Document".

The model already receives file content via `add_file_context()` (which injects `<file>` tags) and has access to the `query_knowledge_bases` builtin tool. This is consistent with how every other feature handler works: folder knowledge, model knowledge, memory, web search, image generation, and code interpreter all skip their legacy injection path when `function_calling == 'native'`.

### Actual Behavior

When a file is uploaded with the default **"Using Focused Retrieval"** mode (i.e. `context` is not `'full'`), **both** paths execute:

1. `add_file_context()` injects `<file>` tags into messages (correct for native FC) - **line 2662**
2. `chat_completion_files_handler()` **also** runs - **line 2697-2702** - because it is only gated by `file_context_enabled`, not by `function_calling != 'native'`

Inside `chat_completion_files_handler` (line 1870), because `all_full_context` is `False`:
- `generate_queries()` fires (line 1883) - makes an extra LLM call to the **task model** to generate search queries
- `get_sources_from_items()` performs vector search with embeddings (line 1927)
- `apply_source_context_to_messages()` injects the retrieved chunks via the RAG template into the messages (line 2714)

The model receives **redundant, potentially conflicting context**: native `<file>` tags AND legacy RAG-injected chunks. The extra task-model call also adds unnecessary latency.

When the file is switched to **"Use Entire Document"** (`context = 'full'`), the symptom is masked because `all_full_context = True` skips `generate_queries()` - no visible task-model call - though `apply_source_context_to_messages` still injects content.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a model (e.g. GPT-4o, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible model) with **native function calling** enabled in model settings
2. Start a new chat with that model
3. Upload a document (e.g. a PDF) - it defaults to **"Using Focused Retrieval"** (`context` is `undefined`)
4. Send a message asking about the document content
5. Observe in the UI: a "Generating search queries" status appears, and retrieved sources/citations are injected - this is the legacy RAG pipeline running
6. Check backend logs (`GLOBAL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`): you will see both `add_file_context` adding `<file>` tags AND `generate_queries` / `query_collection` executing

**Contrast - other handlers are correctly gated:**
- Toggle the same file to "Use Entire Document" → `generate_queries` is skipped (masked, not fixed)
- Use folder knowledge or model-attached knowledge with the same native FC model → legacy RAG is correctly skipped

### Root Cause

In `backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py`, the `chat_completion_files_handler` call at line 2697 is missing the `function_calling != 'native'` guard that all other handlers have:

```python
# Line 2694-2702 - CURRENT (buggy)
file_context_enabled = (model.get('info', {}).get('meta', {}).get('capabilities') or {}).get('file_context', True)

if file_context_enabled:
    try:
        form_data, flags = await chat_completion_files_handler(request, form_data, extra_params, user)
        sources.extend(flags.get('sources', []))
    except Exception as e:
        log.exception(e)
```

**Every other handler** has this pattern:

| Handler | Guard |
|---|---|
| Folder files (line 2247) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| Model knowledge (line 2261) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| Memory (line 2338) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| Web search (line 2343) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| Image generation (line 2348) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| Code interpreter (line 2356) | `if function_calling != 'native'` ✅ |
| **chat_completion_files_handler (line 2697)** | **Missing** ❌ |

### Logs & Screenshots

With `GLOBAL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the log shows both paths executing for the same request:

```
# Native FC path (correct)
add_file_context: adding <file> tags for chat_id=...

# Legacy RAG path (should be skipped)
generate_queries: generating search queries...
query_doc_with_hybrid_search: ...
apply_source_context_to_messages: injecting RAG template...
```

### Additional Information

The fix should add the same guard to the files handler:

```python
if file_context_enabled and metadata.get('params', {}).get('function_calling') != 'native':
```

This would make the files handler consistent with all other handlers in the middleware pipeline.

title: feat: Introduce a proper full-text search index for chat history (Postgres tsvector + SQLite FTS5)
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions for similar requests. I have found none that is comparable to my request.

### Verify Feature Scope

- [x] I have read through and understood the scope definition for feature requests in the Issues section. I believe my feature request meets the definition and belongs in the Issues section instead of the Discussions.

### Problem Description

Today, chat search (`Chats.get_chats_by_user_id_and_search_text` in `backend/open_webui/models/chats.py`) does a full JSON expansion and `LIKE '%term%'` scan on every search. This is:

- **Slow** - O(total chat content) per query; multi-second searches on a few thousand chats.
- **Memory-heavy** - full JSON arrays are materialized; OOM-kills small Docker containers.
- **Inaccurate** - single literal substring on string-typed `content` only (see sibling accuracy issue).

No FTS index exists. There is no index on `Chat.title`. There is no `search_vector` column. The only relevant indexes today are:

```python
Index('folder_id_idx', 'folder_id'),
Index('user_id_pinned_idx', 'user_id', 'pinned'),
Index('user_id_archived_idx', 'user_id', 'archived'),
Index('updated_at_user_id_idx', 'updated_at', 'user_id'),
Index('folder_id_user_id_idx', 'folder_id', 'user_id'),
```

### Desired Solution you'd like
Add a dedicated, maintained full-text search index for chat content, using the database's native FTS capabilities.

### Postgres
1. Add a `chat_search` table (or generated column) populated on chat insert/update:

   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE chat_search (
       chat_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES chat(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
       user_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
       title      TEXT,
       content    TEXT,                       -- flattened text from all messages
       updated_at BIGINT NOT NULL,
       search_vector tsvector
           GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
               setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(title, '')),   'A') ||
               setweight(to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(content, '')), 'B')
           ) STORED
   );
   CREATE INDEX chat_search_vector_idx ON chat_search USING GIN (search_vector);
   CREATE INDEX chat_search_user_updated_idx ON chat_search (user_id, updated_at DESC);
   ```

2. (Optional) `pg_trgm` GIN index on `title` for substring/typo-tolerant title matches:
   ```sql
   CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
   CREATE INDEX chat_title_trgm_idx ON chat_search USING GIN (title gin_trgm_ops);
   ```

3. Query:
   ```sql
   SELECT chat_id
   FROM chat_search
   WHERE user_id = :user_id
     AND search_vector @@ websearch_to_tsquery('simple', :q)
   ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_vector, websearch_to_tsquery('simple', :q)) DESC,
            updated_at DESC
   LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset;
   ```

### SQLite
1. Add an FTS5 virtual table:
   ```sql
   CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE chat_fts USING fts5(
       chat_id UNINDEXED,
       user_id UNINDEXED,
       title,
       content,
       tokenize = 'unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
   );
   ```
2. Query with `MATCH` + `bm25()`:
   ```sql
   SELECT chat_id
   FROM chat_fts
   WHERE chat_fts MATCH :q AND user_id = :user_id
   ORDER BY bm25(chat_fts, 5.0, 1.0)
   LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset;
   ```

### Index maintenance
Populate/update the index in the model layer (preferred - works for both dialects without DB triggers):

- On `Chats.insert_new_chat`, `update_chat_by_id_and_user_id`, `upsert_message_to_chat_by_id_and_message_id`, `delete_chat_by_id`, etc., (re)compute the flattened `content` string from all messages (including array-shaped multimodal `content` parts → extract `.text`) and upsert/delete the corresponding `chat_search` / `chat_fts` row.
- Provide an Alembic migration that backfills the index for existing rows in batches.

### Flattening rule (shared)
Given `chat.chat.messages`, the `content` text used for indexing should be:
- string content → as-is
- list content → concatenate all parts where `type in ('text', 'tool_result', 'thinking')` using their `.text`/`.content`/`.value` field
- ignore `image_url`, raw base64, and tool argument JSON

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: issue: PDF upload fails in temporary chat on Safari
body: ### Check Existing Issues - [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues. - [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions. - [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items (your issue might already be addressed on the development branch!). - [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI. ### Installation Method Pip Install ### Open WebUI Version v0.9.5 ### Ollama Version (if applicable) _No response_ ### Operating System macOS Tahoe 26.5 ### Browser (if applicable) Safari 26.5 (bug reproduced) / Firefox Developer Edition 152.0 (works correctly) ### Confirmation - [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`. - [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama. - [x] I have included the browser console logs. - [x] I have included the Docker container logs. - [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.** - [x] I have clearly **listed every relevant configuration, custom setting, environment variable, and command-line option that influences my setup** (such as Docker Compose overrides, .env values, browser settings, authentication configurations, etc). - [x] I have documented **step-by-step reproduction instructions that are precise, sequential, and leave nothing to interpretation**. My steps: - Start with the initial platform/version/OS and dependencies used, - Specify exact install/launch/configure commands, - List URLs visited, user input (incl. example values/emails/passwords if needed), - Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed, - Include any files or environmental changes, - Identify the expected and actual result at each stage, - Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue. ### Expected Behavior Uploading a PDF file in a temporary chat session should extract its text content client-side and inject it into the conversation, as intended by the feature introduced in commit `8d84b4c2a4` ("enh/refac: temp chat file upload behaviour"). ### Actual Behavior In temporary chat, an error toast appears immediately after dropping a PDF: `TypeError: undefined is not a function (near '...n of e...')` The file is not attached to the conversation. The same PDF uploads and is processed correctly when temporary chat is disabled. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Install Open WebUI v0.9.5 via `pip install open-webui` on Python 3.12, macOS 26.5. 2. Start the server. 3. Open the app in Safari. 4. Enable **Temporary Chat** 5. Drag-and-drop a PDF file into the chat input. 6. Observe: the error toast appears and the file is not attached. 7. Disable Temporary Chat and repeat step 5 with the same PDF: upload succeeds. ### Logs & Screenshots The `TypeError` is caught by `.catch()` in `uploadFileHandler` and surfaced only as toasts, so no uncaught exception appears in the browser console. Toast message visible in UI (screenshot attached): "Échec de l'extraction du contenu du fichier : TypeError: undefined is not a function (near '...n of e...')" ### Additional Information ### Root Cause The crash occurs in `extractPdfText()` (`src/lib/utils/index.ts`, introduced by commit `49e045ea3`) at the `page.getTextContent()` call. pdfjs [PR mozilla/pdf.js#20648](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/20648) ("Convert `PDFPageProxy.prototype.getTextContent` to an asynchronous method", merged 2026-02-12) replaced the previous `.getReader()`-based loop with: ```js for await (const value of readableStream) { ... } // pdf.mjs:15030 ``` Confirmed with Safari's debugger paused on exception: the throw occurs at exactly this line. `for await...of` on a `ReadableStream` requires `ReadableStream.prototype[Symbol.asyncIterator]`, which Safari 26.5 does not implement: ```js new ReadableStream()[Symbol.asyncIterator] // is undefined in Safari 26.5 console ``` The loop therefore throws `TypeError: undefined is not a function` immediately. This is caught by `.catch()` in `uploadFileHandler` and displayed as two error toasts. ### Only on temporary chat In normal mode, extraction is server-side via `POST /api/v1/files/` (PyPDFLoader by default). The client-side `extractContentFromFile()` path is only reached in temporary chat mode. ### Only on Safari Firefox Developer Edition 152.0 and Chrome both implement `ReadableStream[Symbol.asyncIterator]`. In Safari, this feature has been tracked since 2019 in WebKit bug #194379. A fix was committed to WebKit main on December 5, 2025 and first appeared in Safari Technology Preview 234, but has not shipped in any stable Safari release: it is absent from the [Safari 26.5 release notes](https://webkit.org/blog/17938/webkit-features-for-safari-26-5). ### Suggested fix add a `Symbol.asyncIterator` polyfill for `ReadableStream` before calling pdfjs, e.g. at the top of `ensurePDFjsLoaded()`. This is minimal, does not change pdfjs API usage, and becomes a no-op once Safari ships the feature natively. ```ts if (!ReadableStream.prototype[Symbol.asyncIterator]) { ReadableStream.prototype[Symbol.asyncIterator] = async function* () { const reader = this.getReader(); try { while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) return; yield value; } } finally { reader.releaseLock(); } }; } ``` An alternative would be to rewrite `extractPdfText()` using `page.streamTextContent().getReader()` and an explicit `while` loop instead of `page.getTextContent()`, which would bypass the `for await...of` without a polyfill. However, this is exactly the implementation that pdfjs' [PR mozilla/pdf.js#20648](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/20648) replaced. --- Notes: - `pdfjs-dist` version pinned in `package.json`: `^5.4.149`. - Related upstream bugs: [mozilla/pdf.js#20973](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/20973) (same crash in the pdfjs legacy build), [bugs.webkit.org/194379](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=194379) (WebKit tracking issue for `ReadableStream[Symbol.asyncIterator]`).

### Expected Behavior

The file should be loaded with a fallback encoding (e.g. Latin-1) so the content is available for retrieval, even if the file is not valid UTF-8.

### Actual Behavior

Two failures occur in the processing pipeline:

### 1. `_is_text_file` misclassifies non-UTF-8 text files as binary

**File:** `backend/open_webui/routers/files.py`, lines 70-88

The function tries `chunk.decode('utf-8')` to determine if a file is text. When the file contains Latin-1/Windows-1252 bytes, this raises `UnicodeDecodeError` and the function returns `False`. This causes files with mis-detected content types (e.g. `.ts` files typed as `video/mp2t`) to fail re-classification as `text/plain`.

### 2. `TextLoader` autodetection fails or times out (primary issue)

**File:** `backend/open_webui/retrieval/loaders/main.py`, lines 503-506 (and other locations: 280, 332, 429, 441, 445)

All `TextLoader` instantiations use `autodetect_encoding=True`:

```python
loader = TextLoader(file_path, autodetect_encoding=True)
```

The langchain `TextLoader` fallback flow is:

1. Try `open(file, encoding=None)` - on Linux this defaults to UTF-8, which fails on Latin-1 bytes
2. Fall back to `chardet.detect_all()` via `detect_file_encodings()` - this either:
   - Returns low-confidence, incorrect encodings (e.g. MacRoman with 0.73 confidence for Windows-1252 content), which also fail to decode
   - Times out after 5 seconds (the hardcoded langchain default), raising a `TimeoutError`
3. No further fallback exists - the document fails to load entirely

The error logged is:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xdc in position 25129: invalid continuation byte
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or obtain a `.txt` or `.csv` file that contains non-UTF-8 characters (e.g. German umlauts like Ü, ö, ä encoded in Latin-1 / Windows-1252 - bytes `0xdc`, `0xf6`, `0xe4`, `0xfc`, etc.)
2. Upload the file via the Open WebUI file upload
3. Observe the upload appears to succeed (file shows in the file list)
4. Try to reference the file in a chat - the LLM cannot access the file content
## Analysis

- Files with mixed ASCII + legacy-encoded non-ASCII bytes (common in industrial/exported text files from Windows environments) are not handled
- `chardet` is unreliable for files that are mostly ASCII with sparse non-UTF-8 bytes - confidence is low and detection is slow
- A Latin-1 fallback would always succeed (every byte 0x00-0xFF is valid Latin-1), and OWUI already applies `ftfy.fix_text()` post-load (line 241 of `loaders/main.py`) which can clean up mojibake from mixed-encoding content

## Suggested Fix

In `Loader._get_loader()` (`backend/open_webui/retrieval/loaders/main.py`), catch the failure from `TextLoader(autodetect_encoding=True)` and retry with `encoding='latin-1'`:

```python
try:
    loader = TextLoader(file_path, autodetect_encoding=True)
    docs = loader.load()
except (UnicodeDecodeError, RuntimeError):
    loader = TextLoader(file_path, encoding="latin-1")
    docs = loader.load()
```

Additionally, in `_is_text_file()` (`backend/open_webui/routers/files.py`), fall back to Latin-1 decoding when UTF-8 fails:

```python
try:
    chunk.decode('utf-8')
    return True
except UnicodeDecodeError:
    try:
        chunk.decode('latin-1')
        return True
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return False
```

title: Feature: FunASR as local STT backend (OpenAI-compatible, 13x faster than Whisper)
body:
## Summary

Open WebUI supports Whisper for speech-to-text. [FunASR](https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR) (16.5K stars, MIT) provides an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint that's significantly faster and runs well on CPU - making it ideal as a local STT backend.

## Why this matters for Open WebUI users

| | Whisper | FunASR |
|---|---|---|
| GPU speed | 13x realtime | **170x realtime** |
| CPU speed | ❌ Too slow for interactive | **17x realtime** (usable!) |
| API compatibility | OpenAI native | **OpenAI-compatible** |
| Speaker diarization | ❌ | ✅ built-in |
| Languages | 57 | 50+ |
| License | MIT | MIT |

The CPU performance is the key differentiator - Open WebUI users who self-host on CPU-only machines (common for home servers) can get fast local STT without needing a GPU.

## How it works today (zero code changes needed)

FunASR already exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```bash
pip install funasr fastapi uvicorn python-multipart
funasr-server --device cpu
# → http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions
```

If Open WebUI allows configuring a custom STT base URL (like it does for LLM backends), users can point it to `http://localhost:8000/v1` and it works immediately - same request/response format as OpenAI's transcription API.

## Suggestion

- Document FunASR as a supported local STT option in the docs/wiki
- Or add it as a preset in the STT backend settings (alongside OpenAI Whisper API)

No code change is strictly required since the API is compatible - it's mainly a documentation/discoverability improvement.

Deploy Open WebUI via Docker on port 8080. 2. Add OpenRouter as OpenAI-compatible provider. 3. Create custom model preset `autoopenrouter`: - Base model: `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free` - **Function Calling**: Native - Enable: Vision, Web Search, File Upload, Tools, etc. 4. Upload any image (PNG/JPEG) and ask "What's in this image?" 5. Observe: - Model calls `view_knowledge_file(file_id)` - Tool returns: `{"id": "...", "filename": "image.png", "content": "", ...}` ### Logs & Screenshots **Key server log**: ``` open_webui.routers.files:upload_file_handler:216 - file.content_type: image/png False POST /api/v1/files/?process=false HTTP/1.1 200 ``` **Tool response** (empty content): ``` {"id": "", "filename": "image.png", "content": "", "updated_at": ..., "created_at": ...} ``` ### Additional Information **Related Issue**: [#20851](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/20851) - `view_knowledge_file` builtin tool not injected in Native mode. In our case the tool IS available but returns empty content. **Root Cause Analysis**: In Native mode + OpenRouter, images are uploaded with `?process=false` and stored only as file references (no base64 conversion, no disk write). `view_knowledge_file` can find the file metadata but cannot return the actual binary content to a remote API like OpenRouter. The image data is never made available during the request lifecycle. **Attempted Workarounds** (all failed): 1. Haervwe Semantic Router Filter v2.0.1 - routing works, image still empty 2. Set `function_calling = "default"` in Filter - images work but web search broken 3. Read image from `app.state.FILES` in Filter inlet - not populated at inlet time 4. Read from disk via `Files.get_file_metadata_by_id()` - `process=false` means no disk write 5. HTTP API `GET /api/v1/files/{fid}/content` - returns 200 but empty body 6. Custom minimal Filter changing only `body["model"]` - same issue (inherits native behavior) 7. Embed image instructions in system message - model reads prompt, not actual image **Workaround**: Maintain two separate model presets and switch manually: - **Model A**: Native mode → for text + web search (don't send images) - **Model B**: Default mode → for image analysis (web search unavailable) **Reproduction Repository**: https://github.com/YangObscurity/openwebui-native-image-deadlock

title: feat: bidirectional visual plugin system
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions for similar requests. I have found none that is comparable to my request.

### Verify Feature Scope

- [x] I have read through and understood the scope definition for feature requests in the Issues section. I believe my feature request meets the definition and belongs in the Issues section instead of the Discussions.

### Problem Description

Currently, Open WebUI's plugin system (Functions / Pipelines) is server-side Python logic only. There is no native way to embed an interactive frontend page that maintains its own visual state and communicates bidirectionally with the model.
Complex structured inputs - such as node graphs, blueprints, form wizards, or spatial layouts - are extremely cumbersome to express in plain text. Users are forced to describe visual intent verbally, which is imprecise, slow, and error-prone. Equally, the model has no way to drive a visual canvas via API calls, meaning it cannot assist users with visual decision-making in real time.
In short: there is no bridge between the model's structured reasoning and a user-facing interactive UI, which makes collaborative visual tasks practically impossible within Open WebUI today.

### Desired Solution you'd like

## Feature request: bidirectional visual plugin system

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, Open WebUI's plugin system (Functions / Pipelines) is primarily server-side Python logic. There is no native way to embed an interactive frontend page that can both receive structured output from the model and send structured state back to the model. Complex structured inputs - like node graphs, blueprints, form wizards, or spatial layouts - are cumbersome to express in plain text, and the model cannot drive a visual canvas via API calls.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A **bidirectional visual plugin** system, where:

1. **Plugin registration**: A developer ships a single-page web app (iframe) alongside a manifest (JSON schema + skill/system prompt) that describes:
   - What JSON the model can send to render the UI
   - What API methods the model can call (e.g. `connectNodes(a, b)`, `addNode(type, pos)`)
   - What JSON the UI sends back to the model as `tool_result`

2. **Model → UI channel**: The model calls a tool (e.g. `render_plugin`) with a JSON payload; the plugin page receives it and renders accordingly.

3. **UI → Model channel**: After user interaction (e.g. manually drawing a connection, moving a node), the plugin serialises its state to JSON and returns it as a `tool_result` so the model understands the updated context.

4. **Model → UI API calls**: The model can call named methods exposed by the plugin (via `tool_use`), allowing it to programmatically manipulate the canvas - e.g. suggest connections, highlight nodes, or populate fields.

5. **Bundled skill/system prompt**: The plugin manifest includes a skill snippet injected into the system prompt, which tells the model the plugin's schema, available API methods, and how to interpret returned JSON.

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Using plain Artifacts (HTML rendered in chat): supports model → UI rendering, but has no standardised channel for UI → model state return or model-callable UI APIs.
- MCP (Model Context Protocol): covers model ↔ server tool bidirectionality, but is not designed for frontend UI state management.
- Pipelines: server-side only; no frontend visual canvas.

---

**Use cases**

- Node graph / blueprint editor (e.g. workflow builder, shader graph, dependency mapper)
- Form wizard where the model pre-fills fields and the user corrects them
- Spatial layout tool (e.g. seating plan, floor plan, ER diagram)
- Data table editor with model-assisted column mapping
- Decision tree builder with collaborative model + user branching

---

**Additional context**

This pattern is sometimes called "Embodied Tools" or "Generative UI with bidirectional state". Related prior art:
- Vercel AI SDK Generative UI (model → UI, but no standardised UI → model return)
- Anthropic Artifacts (similar canvas concept, proprietary to Claude.ai)
- MCP protocol (bidirectional, but server-side)

Happy to draft a detailed spec or prototype if there is interest.

### Alternatives Considered

Plain Artifacts / HTML in chat: Supports model → UI rendering, but there is no standardised channel for UI → model state return, and the model cannot call UI methods programmatically.
MCP (Model Context Protocol): Covers bidirectional model ↔ tool communication, but is designed for server-side tools - not for frontend UI state management or visual canvas interaction.
Pipelines: Server-side only. No concept of a frontend visual surface that the model can read from or write to.
Plain text + structured prompting: Users can describe visual structures in text (e.g. JSON node lists), but this is slow, error-prone, and completely bypasses the usability advantage of a visual interface.

None of the above support the full loop: model renders UI → user interacts → UI returns state → model reasons on updated state → model calls UI API → repeat.

### Actual Behavior

 The builtin tool functions declare int/Optional[int] type hints but never coerce the actual runtime values. When the model passes a numeric parameter as a string, any comparison or arithmetic on that value raises:


    TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'


    This crashes the tool call and the model receives an error response instead of search results.

### Steps to Reproduce

    1. Configure a model with native function calling enabled (Admin Panel → Function Calling = Native)
    2. Enable SearXNG web search
    3. In a chat, ask the model to search for something (e.g., "What is the weather in Portland OR?")
    4. The model emits a tool call: search_web(query="Portland Oregon weather today", count=1)
    5. If the model passes count as the string "1" in the tool call JSON, the min(count, max_count) comparison on line 233 of builtin.py crashes with TypeError

 2026-06-03 02:15:56.762 | ERROR | open_webui.tools.builtin:search_web:245 - search_web error: '<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'

        tool_result = await tool_function(**tool_function_params)

 20 builtin tool functions in backend/open_webui/tools/builtin.py are affected - any that accept int or Optional[int] parameters and use them in comparisons, arithmetic, or slicing:

    - calculate_timestamp: days_ago + (weeks_ago * 7), months_ago > 0, years_ago > 0
    - search_notes, search_chats, search_channel_messages: start_timestamp * 1_000_000_000, end_timestamp * 1_000_000_000

- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

Opening a Knowledge Base - and any background polling for in-flight files - should issue a lookup whose cost scales with the number of pending files, not with the total extracted document text in the file table. With a large file table this query should remain an index lookup, and the polling that drives it should not be able to stack requests on top of each other. A KB with no genuinely-processing files should generate negligible DB load.

This is the same pathology I reported in #25082, on a different (newly-added in 0.9.6) endpoint.

### Actual Behavior

The new `GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files/pending endpoint` (0.9.6) is backed by `Files.get_pending_files_for_knowledge` in `backend/open_webui/models/files.py`, which runs:

```
SELECT ... FROM file
WHERE CAST(((meta -> 'data') ->> 'knowledge_id') AS VARCHAR) = $1
  AND CAST((data ->> 'status') AS VARCHAR) IN ('pending','processing')
  AND file.id NOT IN (SELECT file_id FROM knowledge_file WHERE knowledge_id = $2);
```

All three predicates are unindexed JSON expressions, so every call is a full sequential scan of file. Since file.data holds the full extracted content of every document, that table is multi-GB on a large deployment, a plain COUNT with this filter took 1m43s for me.

The frontend amplifies it. In `src/lib/components/chat/Knowledge/KnowledgeBase.svelte`, `init()` calls the endpoint on every KB page load, and if anything is pending it starts `setInterval(..., 5000)` with an async callback and no overlap guard so it re-fires every 5s regardless of whether the previous request finished. When the query takes minutes, the polls pile up: I saw 30+ concurrent parallel seq-scans of file at once, one set per open tab.

On my deployment (5k users, hundreds of thousands of files) this pinned Aurora Serverless v2 at 100% of 120 ACU and took the instance down. I had to roll back to 0.9.5.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Stand up Open WebUI v0.9.6 backed by Postgres, with a non-trivial file table (large extracted data.content).
2. Open a Knowledge Base in Workspace → Knowledge; open it in a few tabs.
3. Watch the Postgres logs / pg_stat_activity. Each init() and each 5s interval fires SELECT public.file... as a full seq-scan; with multiple tabs they stack into many concurrent parallel scans.
4. Observe DB CPU / ACU climb to saturation; under a real file table each scan takes minutes.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (server), `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.9.6`

### Browser (if applicable)

Any (reproduced in Chrome 137 and with plain `curl`)

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.
- [x] I have included the Docker container logs.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.**
- [x] I have clearly **listed every relevant configuration, custom setting, environment variable, and command-line option that influences my setup.**
- [x] I have documented **step-by-step reproduction instructions that are precise, sequential, and leave nothing to interpretation.**

### Expected Behavior

Opening the chat **"Attach files"** picker fetches a lightweight file *list* (id, filename, meta) - a few KB.

### Actual Behavior

The picker calls `GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50`, and the backend serializes **`data.content` (the full extracted text) of every listed file** into the response. On our instance (165 files, some large PDFs/DOCX):

| Request | Response size | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50` | **63,570,528 bytes (~64 MB)** | 1.96 s |
| `GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50&content=false` | **27,522 bytes (~27 KB)** | 1.54 s |

That is a ~2,300× payload difference for a UI that only renders filenames. The same request is re-issued for every search-input change in the picker, so each picker interaction can transfer hundreds of MB. `GET /api/v1/files/` has the same issue (~23 MB here), affecting other list consumers.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.9.6` (stock config; ours uses pgvector + an OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint, but that is irrelevant - any deployment reproduces it).
2. Upload ~50+ documents with substantial text (multi-MB PDFs/DOCX/XLSX).
3. Open a chat, click **+** → **Attach files** (the in-app file picker, not OS upload).
4. In browser DevTools → Network, observe `GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50` transferring tens of MB. Type in the picker's search box and observe a similarly sized response per query change.

### Root Cause

The backend already supports skipping content - `search_files` has `content: bool = Query(True)` and strips `data.content` when `false` (`backend/open_webui/routers/files.py`, `/search` route). The frontend just never passes it: `searchFiles()` in `src/lib/apis/files/index.ts` builds the query from `filename`, `skip`, `limit` only.

### Suggested Fix

- Pass `content=false` from `searchFiles()` (and `getFiles()` where the caller only renders a list), **or**
- flip the `/search` default to `content=false`, since returning the full extracted text of *all* files by default is rarely the intent of a search/list call (note: it also returns content of other users' files for admins with `BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL`).

Happy to submit a PR for either variant if maintainers indicate the preferred direction.

### Logs

No backend errors - the requests succeed (`200`); the issue is payload size/latency. Container log excerpt showing the picker traffic:

```
GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50 HTTP/1.1" 200
GET /api/v1/files/search?filename=*&skip=0&limit=50 HTTP/1.1" 200   (×8 within one session)
```

### Workaround (for other affected users)

Reverse-proxy level: append `content=false` to `/api/v1/files/search` when the client did not specify `content` explicitly (nginx `set` + conditional `proxy_pass`). Restores instant picker loads without touching the app.

title: bug: Artifact panel does not auto-open for HTML generated by outlet filter functions
body:
## Description

When a filter function's `outlet` hook converts a non-HTML code block (e.g. \`\`\`markdown) to \`\`\`html, the artifact panel does not automatically open on the right side. The user must manually click the code block to trigger it.

For \`\`\`html blocks emitted directly by the LLM during streaming, the panel auto-opens correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a filter function with an `outlet` hook that converts \`\`\`markdown blocks to \`\`\`html (e.g., a markdown-to-HTML document renderer)
2. Send a prompt that triggers the LLM to emit a \`\`\`markdown block
3. After streaming completes, the outlet converts it to \`\`\`html
4. The artifact panel does not open automatically - user must click the code block

## Expected Behavior

The artifact panel should auto-open after the outlet converts the content to \`\`\`html, just like it does for \`\`\`html blocks emitted directly during streaming.

## Root Cause Analysis

`ContentRenderer.svelte` (line ~247) has an `onUpdate` callback that calls `showArtifacts.set(true)` when the markdown renderer processes a code block with `lang="html"`. This fires correctly during the initial streaming render.

However, when the outlet modifies the message content post-stream (converting \`\`\`markdown → \`\`\`html), the markdown renderer's `onUpdate` callback does not re-fire for the new \`\`\`html block. The Svelte reactive system updates the content, but the artifact detection logic in `onUpdate` is not re-triggered.

- Browser: Chrome
- Platform: macOS

title: issue: Input field auto-focuses after each response in call mode, triggering mobile keyboard
body:
## Describe the bug

When using **Call mode** (voice overlay), the chat input field receives focus automatically after every model response finishes. This causes two problems:

1. **Formatting toolbar appears** - if the rich text toolbar is enabled, it pops up after every response, even though it's not needed in hands-free mode.
2. **Mobile keyboard opens** - on Android/iOS PWA, the auto-focus triggers the virtual keyboard every time the assistant finishes speaking, which defeats the purpose of hands-free call mode.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat in **Call mode** (microphone icon → call overlay active)
2. Ask any question via voice
3. Wait for the model to finish responding / TTS to finish playing
4. Observe: the chat input field receives focus automatically

## Expected behavior

In call mode, the input field should **not** receive focus after a response. The user is operating hands-free; auto-focusing the input serves no purpose and actively disrupts the experience (especially on mobile).

## Current behavior

The input receives focus after each response, causing:
- The rich text formatting toolbar to appear
- The mobile virtual keyboard to open (PWA on Android/iOS)

## Code analysis

The codebase already contains a partial fix with an explicit comment in `src/lib/components/chat/Chat.svelte`:

```js
// focus on chat input (skip during voice call to avoid triggering mobile keyboard)
if (!$showCallOverlay) {
    chatInput?.focus();
}
```

However, there are several other `.focus()` calls in `Chat.svelte` and `MessageInput.svelte` that do **not** check `$showCallOverlay`, e.g.:

- `Chat.svelte` ~line 261 (navigateHandler)
- `Chat.svelte` ~line 877 (onMount / init)
- `Chat.svelte` ~line 1386 (model change handler, inside `setTimeout`)
- `MessageInput.svelte` ~line 1088 (onMount)
- `MessageInput.svelte` ~line 1165 (modal close callback)

All of these need the same `if (!$showCallOverlay)` guard.

## Environment

- Open WebUI version: current
- Platform: Desktop + Android PWA
- Browser: Chrome

## Additional context

This issue has existed for a long time and is particularly disruptive on mobile PWA where the keyboard covers half the screen after every single response in what is supposed to be a fully hands-free interaction mode.

My steps: - Start with the initial platform/version/OS and dependencies used, - Specify exact install/launch/configure commands, - List URLs visited, user input (incl. example values/emails/passwords if needed), - Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed, - Include any files or environmental changes, - Identify the expected and actual result at each stage, - Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue. ### Expected Behavior After [PR #24690](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/24690) (merged into v0.9.6), `handle_authorize` should include the `scope` parameter in the OAuth authorize URL when using MCP with OAuth 2.1 (Static) and an IdP that requires scopes (e.g. Azure Entra ID). ### Actual Behavior `handle_authorize` (`open_webui/utils/oauth.py`, ~line 960) generates an authorize URL **without** `scope`, causing the IdP to reject the request (Entra: `AADSTS900144`). Debug logging at `handle_authorize` proves: ``` client_info.scope=None client_kwargs={'follow_redirects': True, 'token_endpoint_auth_method': 'client_secret_post'} kwargs={} ``` The scope is correctly discovered from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and correctly built in `get_oauth_client_info_with_static_credentials` ([PR #24690](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/pull/24690)), but is **not present** in `client_info` when `handle_authorize` runs. Hardcoding `kwargs["scope"]` before `authorize_redirect` immediately resolves the issue (Entra accepts the request). Additionally, `_preflight_authorization_url` calls `create_authorization_url(redirect_uri=redirect_uri)` **without** `scope`, which causes the preflight check against Entra to fail with the same error before `handle_authorize` is even reached. **File**: `open_webui/utils/oauth.py` The scope is lost in the persistence/loading chain: 1. **Build** ✅ - `get_oauth_client_info_with_static_credentials` (~line 529) builds `OAuthClientInformationFull` with `scope` from `get_protected_resource_metadata` (PR #24690) 2. **Persist** ✅ - The `OAuthClientInformationFull` object is encrypted and stored as a blob in the connection config (`info.oauth_client_info`) 3. **Load** ❌ - `ensure_client_from_config` (~line 691) calls `resolve_oauth_client_info` which decrypts the blob into a dict, then constructs `OAuthClientInformationFull(**dict)`. If the blob was created **before** PR #24690, the `scope` field is missing from the dict → `scope=None` 4. **Register** ❌ - `add_client` (~line 633) only sets `client_kwargs.scope` if `oauth_client_info.scope` is truthy: `**({'scope': oauth_client_info.scope} if oauth_client_info.scope else {})` 5. **Authorize** ❌ - `handle_authorize` (~line 960) only sets `kwargs['scope']` if `client_info.scope` is truthy → URL has no scope **Key finding**: Deleting the MCP server from the DB and re-registering does **not** fix the issue. `client_info.scope` remains `None` at runtime. This suggests that either: - Re-registration does not trigger `get_oauth_client_info_with_static_credentials` to rebuild the encrypted blob, or - The serialization/encryption of the `OAuthClientInformationFull` object does not include the `scope` field **Secondary issue**: `_preflight_authorization_url` (~line 719) does not pass `scope` to `create_authorization_url` at all - it only passes `redirect_uri`. For IdPs that require scope (like Entra), this causes the preflight to fail before `handle_authorize` is ever reached. ### Steps to Reproduce ## Environment: **OWUI Setup**: Open WebUI v0.9.6 with Docker, PostgreSQL, hosted with Azure Container Apps **MCP Server**: Any MCP server behind Azure Entra ID OAuth 2.1 that exposes `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` with `scopes_supported` ## Steps 1. Admin Panel → Settings → Integrations → Add MCP Server (Streamable HTTP) 2. Auth type: OAuth 2.1 (Static) - provide `client_id`, `client_secret`, OAuth server URL pointing to Entra 3. Save and register 4. Open a chat → enable the MCP tool → click to authenticate 5. **Result**: Authentication to Entra fails with `AADSTS900144` (scope missing) ## Verification Add the following before `authorize_redirect` in `handle_authorize` (`open_webui/utils/oauth.py`, ~line 960): ```python log.error(f'client_info.scope={client_info.scope!r} client_kwargs={getattr(client, "client_kwargs", None)!r} kwargs={kwargs!r}') ``` ### Logs & Screenshots Error, when activating the MCP Server: ### Additional Information - Related: PR #24690 fixed the scope discovery in get_oauth_client_info_with_static_credentials but did not address the persistence gap where the scope is lost between build and runtime load - Related: Issue #24730 was closed as fixed by PR #24690, but the fix is incomplete - Workaround: Hardcoding kwargs["scope"] = "" before authorize_redirect in handle_authorize resolves the issue immediately - Suggested fix areas: 1. `ensure_client_from_config`: When loading a client from the encrypted blob, re-discover the scope from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` if `scope` is missing 2. `_preflight_authorization_url`: Pass `scope` (and `resource`) to `create_authorization_url` 3. `handle_authorize`: Fallback scope recovery if `client_info.scope` is None

title: bug: AI note edits via replace_note_content silently lost when note is open in editor
body:

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.
- [x] I have included the Docker container logs.

- Start with the initial platform/version/OS and dependencies used,
- Specify exact install/launch/configure commands,
- List URLs visited, user input (incl. example values/emails/passwords if needed),
- Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed,
- Include any files or environmental changes,
- Identify the expected and actual result at each stage,
- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

When the AI uses `replace_note_content` to edit a note, the new content should persist in the editor. Subsequent user keystrokes should not alter the content the AI wrote.


### Actual Behavior

The tool returns `{"status":"success"}` and `view_note` immediately shows the new text - but as soon as the user types any character in the open editor, the AI's edit vanishes and the original content is restored.

Restarting the server temporarily reveals the edit until the note is opened again.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a note in the editor and type some content.
2. In a chat, ask the AI to rewrite the note using the `replace_note_content` built-in tool.
3. Observe that the tool returns success and `view_note` shows the new text.
4. Without closing the note tab, type any character in the editor.
5. The editor reverts to the original content. The AI's edit is gone.

## PoC

Fully self-contained, headless reproduction - no browser needed. The script authenticates, writes via the API as the tool does, then emits the same socket event a browser sends on a keystroke.

`docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    environment:
      WEBUI_SECRET_KEY: "poc-secret-key-12345"
      DEFAULT_USER_ROLE: "admin"
      ENABLE_SIGNUP: "true"
      OLLAMA_BASE_URL: ""
    volumes:
      - owui-data:/app/backend/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "--fail", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 30
      start_period: 30s

  test:
    image: python:3.12-slim
    volumes:
      - ./test_bug.py:/test_bug.py:ro
    command: >
      bash -c "pip install --quiet requests 'python-socketio[client]' && python /test_bug.py"
    environment:
      WEBUI_URL: "http://open-webui:8080"
    depends_on:
      open-webui:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  owui-data:
```

`test_bug.py`:

```python
import os, sys, time
import requests, socketio

BASE_URL         = os.environ.get("WEBUI_URL", "http://localhost:3000")
EMAIL            = "poc@example.com"
PASSWORD         = "Poc123456!"
ORIGINAL_CONTENT = {"md": "# Original\nOriginal content."}
LLM_CONTENT      = {"md": "# LLM Edit\nLLM wrote this."}
STALE_YJS_STATE  = {"md": ORIGINAL_CONTENT["md"] + "\n\nUser added a line."}

# Auth: signin first, signup on first run then signin again
resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/auths/signin", json={"email": EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD})
if not resp.ok:
    requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/auths/signup", json={"email": EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD, "name": "PoC"})
    resp = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/auths/signin", json={"email": EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD})
token = resp.json()["token"]
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
print("[PASS] authenticated")

# Setup: create note with full content, then simulate LLM tool write
note_id = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/notes/create", headers=headers,
    json={"title": "PoC", "data": {"content": ORIGINAL_CONTENT}}).json()["id"]
requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/notes/{note_id}/update", headers=headers,
    json={"title": "PoC", "data": {"content": LLM_CONTENT}})
print(f"[PASS] note created, LLM edit written: {note_id}")

# Verify LLM's edit reached the DB before Yjs kills it
content = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/notes/{note_id}", headers=headers).json()["data"]["content"]
if content["md"] != LLM_CONTENT["md"]:
    sys.exit("[FAIL] LLM edit did not reach DB")
print("[INFO] LLM edit in DB")

# Browser emits ydoc:document:update on every keystroke (Collaboration.ts doc.on('update')).
# The Yjs doc was never told about the LLM edit, so it still holds ORIGINAL_CONTENT.
# 'data' carries the full stale Yjs doc state -> document_save_handler writes it back.
sio = socketio.Client()
sio.connect(BASE_URL, socketio_path="/ws/socket.io", transports=["websocket"], auth={"token": token})
sio.emit("ydoc:document:join", {"document_id": f"note:{note_id}"})
time.sleep(0.5)  # wait for room join
print("[STEP] Simulating user keystroke - browser sends stale Yjs state")
sio.emit("ydoc:document:update", {"document_id": f"note:{note_id}", "data": {"content": STALE_YJS_STATE}, "update": []})
time.sleep(1.5)  # debounce is 0.5s
sio.disconnect()

content = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/notes/{note_id}", headers=headers).json()["data"]["content"]
if content["md"] == LLM_CONTENT["md"]:
    print("[OK] LLM edit preserved - bug not present")
    sys.exit(0)
print("[BUG] LLM edit overwritten by stale Yjs state")
print(f"  DB has:   {content['md']!r}")
print(f"  Expected: {LLM_CONTENT['md']!r}")
print("\n=== BUG REPRODUCED ===")
sys.exit(1)
```

Run: `docker compose up --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from test`


### Logs & Screenshots

Output:

```
[PASS] authenticated
[PASS] note created, LLM edit written: <id>
[INFO] LLM edit in DB
[STEP] Simulating user keystroke - browser sends stale Yjs state
[BUG] LLM edit overwritten by stale Yjs state
  DB has:   '# Original\nOriginal content.\n\nUser added a line.'
  Expected: '# LLM Edit\nLLM wrote this.'

=== BUG REPRODUCED ===
````

### Additional Information

## Root Cause

Note content lives in two places that never sync on the AI write path:

- **DB** (`note.data`) - what REST reads and what `replace_note_content` writes.
- **Yjs CRDT** (`YDOC_MANAGER`, in-memory or Redis) - what the open editor treats as source of truth.

`replace_note_content` writes only the DB. The open editor still holds old content in Yjs. The next keystroke emits a `ydoc:document:update` carrying the full stale doc state, which `document_save_handler` flushes back to the DB - overwriting the AI's edit. `view_note` reads the DB in the brief window before the flush, so the model sees a false success.

### Failure sequence

```
T0    replace_note_content(note_id, "new text")
        → Notes.update_note_by_id → DB content.md = "new text";  returns success

T1    user types one char in open editor
        Collaboration.ts doc.on('update') → emit ydoc:document:update
          with full stale doc state in `data`
        socket/main.py → if data.get('data'): schedule debounced_save (0.5s)

T1+0.5s document_save_handler → Notes.update_note_by_id(stale content)
        AI edit gone.
```

### Affected code

| File | Problem |
|------|---------|
| `tools/builtin.py` (`replace_note_content`) | Writes DB only - no Yjs invalidation, no `note-events` emit |
| `socket/main.py` (`document_save_handler`) | Saves stale client-supplied content from `data['data']` |
| `routers/notes.py` (REST update) | Emits `note-events`; the tool path does not |
| `components/notes/NoteEditor.svelte` (`noteEventHandler`) | Ignores content updates from socket events |




## Proposed Fix

1. **`tools/builtin.py`** - after the DB write, invalidate stale Yjs state via `await YDOC_MANAGER.clear_document(f"note:{note_id}")`, then emit `note-events` so open editors are notified.
2. **`socket/utils.py`** - add `clear_document(document_id)` that drops the Redis key or removes the `self._updates` entry.
3. **`NoteEditor.svelte`** - extend `noteEventHandler` to apply content updates (`editor.commands.setContent(...)`), otherwise open editors show stale content until page reload.

## Workaround

Close the note tab before asking the AI to edit it. On tab close, `ydoc:document:leave` clears the Yjs state, so the next open seeds from the DB correctly.

### Expected Behavior

### Description

When an admin disables chat deletion for users (`chat.delete` permission set to `false`), the restriction is correctly enforced when:
- A user tries to delete an individual chat
- A user tries to delete a folder that **directly contains** chat conversations

However, the restriction is **NOT enforced** when a user deletes a **parent/master folder** that contains no direct chats but has **subfolders with chat conversations inside them**. The parent folder is deleted successfully, which cascades and deletes all subfolders and their chats - effectively bypassing the permission entirely.

---



### Expected Behavior

Deleting the Master Folder should be blocked if **any descendant subfolder** contains chats that the user does not have permission to delete.

### Actual Behavior

Deleting the Master Folder succeeds and cascades - silently deleting all subfolders and their chat conversations, bypassing the `chat.delete` permission check.

### Steps to Reproduce

### Steps to Reproduce

1. As an admin, disable chat deletion for users (`Admin Panel → Users → Permissions → Allow Chat Deletion = false`)
2. Log in as a regular (non-admin) user
3. Create a **Master Folder** in the sidebar
4. Inside the Master Folder, create a **Subfolder**
5. Inside the Subfolder, start one or more chat conversations
6. Attempt to delete the **Subfolder** → ✅ Correctly blocked with permission error
7. Attempt to delete the **Master Folder** (which has no direct chats) → ❌ **Deletion succeeds**, wiping out the Subfolder and all its chats

---

### Logs & Screenshots

### Root Cause

In `backend/open_webui/routers/folders.py`, the `delete_folder_by_id` endpoint checks for chats only in the **top-level folder** being deleted:

```python
# Current (buggy) code
if await Chats.count_chats_by_folder_id_and_user_id(id, user.id, db=db):
    chat_delete_permission = await has_permission(
        user.id, 'chat.delete', request.app.state.config.USER_PERMISSIONS, db=db
    )
    if user.role != 'admin' and not chat_delete_permission:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )
```

When the master folder has **zero direct chats**, `count_chats_by_folder_id_and_user_id` returns `0`, the permission block is skipped, and the deletion proceeds - cascading into all subfolders and deleting their chats.

---

### Suggested Fix

Before performing the permission check, collect all descendant folder IDs and check for chats across the **entire subtree**:

```python
# Proposed fix - check chats across all descendant folders
all_folder_ids = await Folders.get_all_descendant_folder_ids(id, user.id, db=db)

for folder_id in all_folder_ids:
    if await Chats.count_chats_by_folder_id_and_user_id(folder_id, user.id, db=db):
        chat_delete_permission = await has_permission(
            user.id, 'chat.delete', request.app.state.config.USER_PERMISSIONS, db=db
        )
        if user.role != 'admin' and not chat_delete_permission:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
                detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
            )
        break  # Permission is user-level; one match is enough
```

---

### Impact

This is a **permission bypass bug**. An admin-enforced restriction on chat deletion can be circumvented by any user simply by organizing chats into subfolders and deleting the parent folder instead.

### Additional Information

_No response_

- Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed,
- Include any files or environmental changes,
- Identify the expected and actual result at each stage,
- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

When Open WebUI registers a client via **RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)** for an
MCP / OAuth 2.1 tool server, the `scope` it sends in the registration request should be derived
from the **resource's** advertised scopes, following the principle of least privilege:

1. the `scope` value from the `WWW-Authenticate` 401 challenge, if present; otherwise
2. the **Protected Resource Metadata** (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, RFC 9728 §2)
   `scopes_supported` - i.e. the scopes specific to *this* protected resource.

This matches the MCP Authorization spec's
[Scope Selection Strategy](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization#scope-selection-strategy)
and is exactly the source already adopted for the **static-credentials** flow in **PR #24690**
("use Protected Resource Metadata scopes in static OAuth 2.1 flow", merged in v0.9.6, closing
#24730 / relating to #23668).

### Actual Behavior

The **DCR flow** still seeds the registration `scope` from the **Authorization Server Metadata**
`scopes_supported` - the full catalog of every scope the AS can grant across **all** resources it
protects - not from the Protected Resource Metadata.

In `backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py`,
`get_oauth_client_info_with_dynamic_client_registration()` fetches the PRM but **ignores**
`resource_metadata.scopes_supported`, and instead does (current `main`, commit `f2e1aa1`, ~L448-452):

```python
resource_metadata = await get_protected_resource_metadata(oauth_server_url)  # PRM fetched...
resource = resource_metadata.resource
discovery_urls = resource_metadata.get_discovery_urls(oauth_server_url)
for url in discovery_urls:
    ...
    oauth_server_metadata = OAuthMetadata.model_validate(await ...json())
    ...
    if (
        oauth_client_metadata.scope is None
        and oauth_server_metadata.scopes_supported is not None       # <-- AS catalog
    ):
        oauth_client_metadata.scope = ' '.join(oauth_server_metadata.scopes_supported)
```

`resource_metadata.scopes_supported` (PRM) is never consulted here. The space-joined AS
`scopes_supported` is then serialized into the registration POST body (`model_dump(...)` →
`session.post(registration_url, json=registration_data, ...)`).

Consequences:

- **Over-broad scope request (least-privilege violation).** Per RFC 8414 §2, AS `scopes_supported`
  is "a list of the OAuth 2.0 `scope` values that this authorization server supports" - a catalog,
  RECOMMENDED and explicitly non-exhaustive ("Servers MAY choose not to advertise some supported
  scope values"). It is not a recommendation of what a client should request, and it may include
  scopes belonging to entirely different resources/APIs behind the same AS. RFC 9728 §2 defines PRM
  `scopes_supported` as the scopes "used in authorization requests to request access to **this**
  protected resource," and its security guidance says the client "SHOULD still follow OAuth best
  practices and request tokens with as limited a scope as possible."
- **Inconsistent with the static-credentials flow**, which #24690 already moved to PRM scopes. The
  DCR path is the mirror image of the bug fixed in #23668 / #24690, just in a different function.
- Because the registered `scope` becomes the client's stored `scope` (the DCR-response `scope`,
  echoed/narrowed by the AS), it subsequently drives the `scope` query param of the
  `/oauth/clients/{client_id}/authorize` redirect - so the over-broad value can propagate into the
  actual authorization request when the AS does not narrow it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Stand up (or point Open WebUI at) an MCP server acting as an OAuth 2.1 resource server that:
   - serves Protected Resource Metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` with a narrow,
     resource-specific `scopes_supported` (e.g. `["mcp:tools.read"]`), and
   - delegates to an Authorization Server whose
     `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` advertises a **broad** `scopes_supported`
     (e.g. `["openid","profile","email","offline_access","admin","billing:write", ...]`) supporting
     **Dynamic Client Registration** (a `registration_endpoint`).
2. In Open WebUI, add the MCP/tool server with OAuth 2.1 + Dynamic Client Registration (no static
   client credentials), triggering the DCR flow.
3. Observe the outgoing **registration request** (`POST` to the `registration_endpoint`) - capture
   it via the AS logs, a proxy (mitmproxy/Burp), or container logs.

### Logs & Screenshots

Observed registration request body (`scope` populated from AS `scopes_supported`, not PRM):

```json
{
  "client_name": "Open WebUI",
  "redirect_uris": ["https://<webui>/oauth/clients/<id>/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "scope": "openid profile email offline_access admin billing:write ..."  // <-- whole AS catalog
}
```

Expected (`scope` from PRM `scopes_supported`):

```json
{
  "scope": "mcp:tools.read"
}
```

### Additional Information

**Root cause:** `get_oauth_client_info_with_dynamic_client_registration()` in
`backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py` derives the DCR `scope` from AS `scopes_supported` while the
PRM (already fetched in the same function) is the spec-correct source.

**Suggested fix** (mirrors PR #24690): prefer the PRM `scopes_supported` for the DCR registration
`scope`, falling back to the AS catalog (or omitting `scope`) only when PRM scopes are absent -
e.g.:

```python
if oauth_client_metadata.scope is None:
    if resource_metadata.scopes_supported:                 # RFC 9728 - resource-specific
        oauth_client_metadata.scope = ' '.join(resource_metadata.scopes_supported)
    elif oauth_server_metadata.scopes_supported is not None:  # fallback: AS catalog
        oauth_client_metadata.scope = ' '.join(oauth_server_metadata.scopes_supported)
```

(Honoring an admin-provided scope override, as discussed in #23668 / #23696, would be a reasonable
addition on top of this.)

**References**
- RFC 7591 §2 (DCR `scope` is an optional client-metadata field) and §3.2.1 (AS MAY replace/return
  registered metadata).
- RFC 8414 §2 - AS `scopes_supported` is a non-exhaustive catalog, not a per-resource request list.
- RFC 9728 §2 + Security Considerations - PRM `scopes_supported` is the per-resource list; request
  as limited a scope as possible.
- MCP Authorization spec - "Scope Selection Strategy" (WWW-Authenticate `scope` → PRM
  `scopes_supported`; least privilege).
- Related prior work on the **static-credentials** flow: #23668 (issue), **#24690** (merged fix),
  #24730, #23696, #24806. This report covers the **DCR** flow, which those did not touch.

body:

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.
- [x] I have included the Docker container logs.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.**
- [x] I have clearly **listed every relevant configuration, custom setting, environment variable and Docker volume/bind mount used in my setup.**

### Description

The admin feedback list endpoint `GET /api/v1/evaluations/feedbacks/list?page=1&limit=5` returns HTTP 502.

The root cause is in `backend/open_webui/models/feedbacks.py`, method `get_feedback_items()` at line 254:

```python
count_result = await db.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(stmt.subquery()))
total = count_result.scalar()
```

The `stmt` at this point is a `select(Feedback, User).join(User, ...)` with potential ORDER BY on JSON fields (e.g., `Feedback.data['model_id'].as_string()`). Wrapping this complex JOIN + JSON-ORDER statement in `.subquery()` and then counting it can produce invalid SQL or cause database errors, especially with PostgreSQL.

### How to reproduce

1. Deploy Open WebUI v0.9.6 with PostgreSQL backend
2. Login as admin
3. Navigate to Admin Panel → 模型评价 → 反馈 (Evaluations → Feedback)
4. The page shows a loading spinner indefinitely
5. Check the API: `GET /api/v1/evaluations/feedbacks/list?page=1&limit=5` returns 502

### Related context

- The user-scoped endpoint `/api/v1/evaluations/feedbacks/user?page=1&limit=5` works fine (returns 200 with `{items:[], total:0}`)
- The leaderboard endpoint also works correctly (returns 200 with 88 entries)
- The bug was introduced in commit `25898116ea` (async DB migration, April 12, 2026) which converted the sync `query.count()` to the async subquery pattern

### Suggested fix

Replace the subquery count with a lightweight count that avoids wrapping the full JOIN + ORDER BY statement:

```python
# Build a separate count statement with just the JOIN and filters, no ORDER BY
count_stmt = (
    select(func.count(Feedback.id))
    .join(User, Feedback.user_id == User.id)
)
# Re-apply only the WHERE filters (not ORDER BY) from the original stmt
if filter:
    model_id = filter.get('model_id')
    if model_id:
        count_stmt = count_stmt.filter(Feedback.data['model_id'].as_string() == model_id)
count_result = await db.execute(count_stmt)
total = count_result.scalar()
```

This mirrors the pattern used in `backend/open_webui/models/knowledge.py` (lines 360-383) where the count query was correctly separated from the main query during the same async migration.

### Related issues

- #22206 (OOM on bulk endpoints) - related but different root cause. That issue is about loading full datasets into memory; this is a SQL generation bug in the count query.

title: issue: Opaque backend errors: file upload fails with "[ERROR: Error uploading file]" when the filename exceeds the filesystem limit (and a proposal for user-readable error handling)
body: ### Check Existing Issues - [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues. - [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions. - [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items (your issue might already be addressed on the development branch!). - [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI. ### Installation Method Docker ### Open WebUI Version 0.9.6 ### Ollama Version (if applicable) _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 26.04 ### Browser (if applicable) _No response_ ### Confirmation - [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`. - [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama. - [x] I have included the browser console logs. - [x] I have included the Docker container logs. - [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.** - [x] I have clearly **listed every relevant configuration, custom setting, environment variable, and command-line option that influences my setup** (such as Docker Compose overrides, .env values, browser settings, authentication configurations, etc). - [x] I have documented **step-by-step reproduction instructions that are precise, sequential, and leave nothing to interpretation**. My steps: - Start with the initial platform/version/OS and dependencies used, - Specify exact install/launch/configure commands, - List URLs visited, user input (incl. example values/emails/passwords if needed), - Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed, - Include any files or environmental changes, - Identify the expected and actual result at each stage, - Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue. ### Expected Behavior When uploading a file whose name is too long to store, the UI should show a clear, actionable error such as: "File name is too long (maximum 218 bytes). Please rename the file and try again." - or the upload should succeed by truncating the on-disk name (the original name is already stored separately in the file record's meta.name). ### Actual Behavior The upload fails with a generic toast in the top-right of the chat page: [ERROR: Error uploading file] The user gets no hint that the filename length is the problem. The real cause (OSError: ENAMETOOLONG) is only visible in the server logs. This is especially confusing for CJK users: because the 255-byte filesystem limit applies to UTF-8 bytes (3 bytes per CJK character), a perfectly normal-looking ~73-character Chinese/Japanese document title triggers the failure. ### Steps to Reproduce Environment: any default Open WebUI install (no special configuration needed). Reproduced on v0.9.6 with the default LocalStorageProvider (STORAGE_PROVIDER unset). S3/GCS/Azure providers are equally affected because they write to local storage first (backend/open_webui/storage/provider.py). 1. Create a small test file with a 250-character name (254 bytes including ".txt"): python3 -c 'open("a"*250 + ".txt", "w").write("test")' (Alternative, CJK variant - 73 chars = 223 bytes: python3 -c 'open("文"*73 + ".txt", "w").write("test")' ) 2. Log in to the Web UI as any user, open a chat with any model. 3. Click the "+" button in the message input → "Upload Files", and select the file created in step 1 (drag-and-drop reproduces it too). 4. Observe the toast "[ERROR: Error uploading file]" appear in the top right; the file chip disappears from the input. API-level reproduction (no UI needed): curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/files/" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@test.txt;filename=$(python3 -c 'print("a"*250+".txt")')" Returns: {"detail": "Error uploading file"} with HTTP 400. Note the threshold: failures begin at original filenames > 218 bytes, not 255, because upload_file_handler (backend/open_webui/routers/files.py) prefixes the stored name with a 36-char UUID + "_" (37 bytes) before LocalStorageProvider writes it with a plain open(), and filename components are capped at 255 bytes on ext4/APFS/NTFS. ### Logs & Screenshots Backend log at the moment of the failed upload (macOS; Errno 36 on Linux): ERROR [open_webui.routers.files] [Errno 63] File name too long: '/app/backend/data/uploads/_aaaaaaaa...aaa.txt' Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../open_webui/routers/files.py", line 286, in upload_file_handler contents, file_path = await asyncio.to_thread(Storage.upload_file, ...) File ".../open_webui/storage/provider.py", line 65, in upload_file with open(file_path, "wb") as f: OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long The exception is caught by the generic `except Exception` block in upload_file_handler (files.py), which returns HTTP 400 with detail "Error uploading file" - the only thing the user ever sees. ### Additional Information This is one instance of a broader pattern. An audit of backend/open_webui/routers/ shows ~169 uses of ERROR_MESSAGES.DEFAULT: ~90 return an opaque stub ("Something went wrong :/" / "Error uploading file") with no way to correlate a user report with server logs, and ~35 pass raw exception text (ERROR_MESSAGES.DEFAULT(e)) into the response - which can leak server-side filesystem paths and other deployment internals to any logged-in user (e.g. in functions.py, retrieval.py, channels.py). Proposed incremental fix (PR available): 1. utils/errors.py - UserFacingError for anticipated failures, plus an errno→message table (ENAMETOOLONG, ENOSPC, EACCES, EROFS, ...) translated by type/errno rather than echoing exception text, so nothing internal can leak. 2. Central exception handlers in main.py - unhandled exceptions log the full traceback with a short reference ID and return "Something went wrong (ref: a1b2c3d4)" so users can report something actionable. 3. First consumer: the upload path - validate filename byte-length up front and reject with a clear 400. 4. Follow-up: migrate the ~35 raw-leak DEFAULT(e) sites to log-and-translate. Frontend impact: none - the frontend renders `detail` verbatim and never branches on its content (verified across src/). Verified fixes manually: 254-byte and CJK names → specific 400 message; normal upload unaffected; read-only uploads dir → "Server storage is not writable."; unhandled exception → 500 with ref ID and no leaked internals.

### Expected Behavior

When PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/openwebui is set at build time and kit.paths.base is configured
in svelte.config.js, all internal auth redirects should navigate to /openwebui/auth,
not /auth. The subpath deployment should be fully functional end-to-end.

### Actual Behavior

After a successful custom build with PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/openwebui, accessing
http://server/openwebui immediately triggers a redirect to http://server/auth?redirect=%2Fopenwebui%2F
which returns 404. The auth redirect uses the wrong (root-relative) path, making subpath
deployment non-functional despite PUBLIC_BASE_PATH being correctly compiled into the build.

Browser console error:
  GET http://172.16.1.x/auth?redirect=%2Fopenwebui%2F  404 (Not Found)


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with Ubuntu 22.04, Docker installed, any web server capable of reverse proxying
   (tested with NGINX Ingress on Kubernetes).

2. Clone Open WebUI:
     git clone https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui.git
     cd open-webui

3. Edit svelte.config.js to add paths.base so SvelteKit knows its base path at compile time:
     kit: {
       adapter: adapter({ pages: 'build', assets: 'build', fallback: 'index.html' }),
       paths: {
         base: process.env.PUBLIC_BASE_PATH || ''
       }
     }

4. Build the frontend with the subpath baked in:
     PUBLIC_BASE_PATH=/openwebui npm run build

5. Start the Open WebUI backend serving the compiled frontend:
     WEBUI_AUTH=false uvicorn main:app  (or via Docker using the built files)

6. Configure a reverse proxy to serve Open WebUI at /openwebui:
     location ~ /openwebui(/|$)(.*) {
       rewrite ^/openwebui(/|$)(.*) /$2 break;
       proxy_pass http://localhost:8080;
     }
   (or equivalent NGINX Ingress with rewrite-target: /$2 and use-regex: true)

7. Open Chrome incognito. Go to http://your-server/openwebui.

8. Open DevTools → Network tab.

9. Observe: browser immediately redirects to http://your-server/auth?redirect=%2Fopenwebui%2F
   → 404 Not Found.


### Logs & Screenshots

Browser console (Chrome DevTools → Console tab):
  GET http://your-server/auth?redirect=%2Fopenwebui%2F  404 (Not Found)
  te  @ /openwebui/_app/immutable/chunks/D0ROBdhw.js:1
  G   @ /openwebui/_app/immutable/chunks/D0ROBdhw.js:1
  await in G
  Pt  @ /openwebui/_app/immutable/chunks/D0ROBdhw.js:1
  qn  @ /openwebui/_app/immutable/chunks/D0ROBdhw.js:1
  (anonymous) @ /openwebui/_app/immutable/nodes/0.4QR9mmZd.js:3

Note: chunk filenames are hashed and will differ per build.


### Additional Information

ROOT CAUSE (identified through source inspection):

The following files use hardcoded absolute paths for auth navigation instead of
SvelteKit's base-aware goto() or the `base` variable from $app/paths:

1. src/routes/+layout.svelte (~line 777):
     location.href = res?.redirect_url ?? '/auth';
   → navigates to /auth instead of /openwebui/auth

2. src/routes/+layout.svelte (~lines 1092, 1098):
     await goto(`/auth?redirect=${encodedUrl}`);
   → SvelteKit's goto() does NOT auto-prepend base. Must be:
     await goto(`${base}/auth?redirect=${encodedUrl}`);

3. src/routes/+layout.svelte (~line 1097):
     if ($page.url.pathname !== '/auth')
   → With base=/openwebui, pathname is /openwebui/auth, so this guard never matches,

     location.href = res?.redirect_url ?? '/auth';

  import { base } from '$app/paths';
