### Expected Behavior

When an upstream provider rejects a request with a 4xx error, the user should receive a message that helps them understand what went wrong, and the server logs should contain the provider's full error body so an administrator can diagnose the problem.

### Actual Behavior

The user sees a bare 400 Bad Request with no explanation. The upstream provider's error body - which contains an actionable message such as "max_tokens must be less than or equal to 16384" - is silently discarded at process_chat. No trace of the upstream error appears in the OWUI logs. The only way to diagnose the problem is to query the provider's API directly outside of OWUI.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Environment**

- Open WebUI version: v0.10.2 (did not manifest on v0.9.6 with the same database configuration - see root cause note below; related behavior reported as far back as v0.3.19 - see [discussion #5219](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/5219))
- Operating system: Debian (Scaleway VPS)
- Backend: Scaleway Generative APIs (https://api.scaleway.ai/v1, OpenAI-compatible)
- Models affected: Qwen 3.5 series, GLM-5.2 (and per #5219, Groq llama-3.1-70b - this is not model-specific)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. In Admin → Settings → Models → Default Parameters, set max_tokens to a value exceeding the provider's per-model ceiling (e.g., 131072 for Scaleway, which caps at 16384-32768 depending on model).
2. Send any chat message from any user account.
3. Observe: the UI displays 400 Bad Request with no further information.
4. Check the upstream provider's API directly - the provider may return a clear, human-readable error message that OWUI never surfaces.

Confirming the root cause: reverting max_tokens to a value within the provider's ceiling (in our case, 16384) immediately resolves the issue. The max_tokens value in models.default_params is applied to every request globally.



### Logs & Screenshots

The OWUI container log contains only the generic aiohttp error - the upstream provider's response body is absent:

```
ERROR [open_webui.routers.openai] 400, message='Bad Request', url='https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/chat/completions'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/backend/open_webui/routers/openai.py", line 1512, in process_chat
    r.raise_for_status()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/aiohttp/client_reqrep.py", line 1093, in raise_for_status
    raise ClientResponseError(
aiohttp.client_exceptions.ClientResponseError: 400, message='Bad Request',
    url='https://api.scaleway.ai/v1/chat/completions'
INFO: 172.17.0.1:0 - "POST /api/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
```

The provider's actual error body - never logged by OWUI - looks like this (retrieved by querying the provider directly):

```
json{
  "error": {
    "message": "max_tokens must be less than or equal to 16384 for model qwen3-235b-a22b",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "invalid_parameter"
  }
}
```

Without the second query, there is no way to determine from OWUI logs alone why the request was rejected.

**Root cause analysis**

This is two separate problems compounding each other:

1. Upstream error bodies are silently discarded.
When process_chat receives a 4xx from the upstream OpenAI-compatible endpoint, it catches the error and returns a generic HTTP 400 to the client without forwarding the provider's response body or writing it to the logs. Users and administrators have no way to learn what the provider actually rejected.

2. Possible regression in how models.default_params.max_tokens is applied in v0.10.x.
The same database configuration (max_tokens: 131072 in models.default_params) did not cause failures on v0.9.6. Something changed in v0.10.x in how this value is passed to upstream OpenAI-compatible APIs - either a code path that previously omitted or capped the value now forwards it verbatim, or the parameter is newly included in request payloads where it wasn't before. I have not traced the exact change; this warrants investigation. The practical effect is that upgrading from v0.9.6 to v0.10.2 can silently break all completions for users who had set a high max_tokens default, with no warning and no actionable error.

**Suggested fix**

When a 4xx response is received from an upstream OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

1. Log the upstream error body at WARN or ERROR level, so administrators can find the provider's actual error message in the server logs without needing external API access. This alone would make the current behavior self-diagnosable.
2. Return a friendlier message to the end user - e.g., "The request was rejected by the model provider. Please contact your Open WebUI administrator for details." A bare 400 Bad Request is not actionable for end users.

Surfacing the raw upstream error body directly to end users may be undesirable in multi-user deployments (it can expose API configuration details), but the error needs to be preserved for admin troubleshooting.

### Additional Information

This pattern was reported in September 2024 in [discussion #5219](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/5219) (Groq + llama-3.1-70b, v0.3.19) and received no response. The underlying error-propagation behavior is provider-agnostic and will recur whenever any OpenAI-compatible backend enforces a ceiling that differs from OWUI's configured defaults.

title: feat: first-class support for BaseRT as a local inference provider
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions and found none comparable to my request.

### Verify Feature Scope

- [x] I believe this feature request is appropriately scoped for the Issues section as described above.

### Problem Description


Open WebUI currently has first-class affordances for two local runtimes: Ollama (full native integration) and llama.cpp (via the `provider` hook on OpenAI-compatible connections - loaded-state badge, model unload, correct reasoning replay).

[BaseRT](https://github.com/basecompute/baseRT) is a local LLM inference runtime for Apple Silicon that serves an OpenAI-compatible API (chat, completions, embeddings, transcription, tool calls). It can already be connected as a generic OpenAI connection, but without a provider identity users lose functionality that the server actually supports:

- **Reasoning content is silently dropped from multi-turn history.** `get_reasoning_format()` returns `None` for unknown providers, so `reasoning_content` - which BaseRT emits and accepts back - is never replayed. Follow-up turns lose the model's prior reasoning.
- **No loaded-state indicator.** BaseRT reports a boolean `loaded` field on `GET /v1/models`, but only `provider == 'llama.cpp'` load states are read, so the green "loaded" dot never appears.
- **No Eject button.** `/api/models/unload` only dispatches Ollama and llama.cpp, even though BaseRT exposes `POST /v1/models/unload`.
- **Wrong connection-type default.** OpenAI connections default to External; a local runtime should default to Local (which also gates local task-model selection).


### Proposed Solution


Add `basert` as a provider option on OpenAI-compatible connections, following the existing `llama.cpp`/`azure` precedent - no new provider stack, no new dependencies, no new settings:

1. **BaseRT** entry in the provider dropdown of the connection modal, defaulting the connection type to Local
2. Generalize the llama.cpp loaded-state helper to also read BaseRT's boolean `loaded` field from `/v1/models`
3. Add a `provider == 'basert'` branch to `/api/models/unload` targeting `POST {base_url}/models/unload`
4. Return `'reasoning_content'` from `get_reasoning_format()` for BaseRT (same as llama.cpp)
5. `"BaseRT"` i18n key across locales

Why it's worth supporting: BaseRT is written directly against Apple's Metal API and reports the highest measured LLM inference throughput on Apple Silicon in published benchmarks ([arXiv:2607.00501](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00501)) ahead of llama.cpp and MLX with M5 tensor-core kernels extending prefill throughput to up to 6.4× over llama.cpp ([M5 technical report](https://www.basecompute.co/BaseRT_M5.pdf)). Its OpenAI compatibility (verified live: SSE streaming with usage chunks, `reasoning_content` deltas, OpenAI-schema tool calls, embeddings, OpenAI-style errors) means the integration surface is a handful of provider-hook branches.


### Alternatives Considered


- **Keep using a generic OpenAI connection** - works for basic chat, but the reasoning-replay loss is a silent correctness issue for reasoning models, and loaded-state/unload remain unavailable despite server support.
- **A full native provider stack (like Ollama's)** - rejected: BaseRT's wire protocol *is* OpenAI, so a parallel router/payload-conversion stack would be all maintenance cost for no functional gain. The `provider` hook mechanism exists precisely for this case.
- **Upstreaming a management UI too (pull/delete models)** - out of scope for now; BaseRT's model management is CLI-only today. A management tab (following the `ManageModelsModal` tab-strip pattern) can follow once BaseRT exposes an HTTP management surface.

### Additional Context


- BaseRT: Apache-2.0 CLI/format/bindings, Apple Silicon (M1+, macOS 14+), models pulled from HuggingFace and converted to its `.base` format; docs at https://docs.basecompute.co
- A PR implementing the proposal is ready: `feat/basert-support` (4 small code changes + i18n, 66 files / 98 insertions, no new dependencies)
- Verified against a live `basert serve` instance; vitest/svelte-check/ruff/eslint/prettier all show zero new findings vs `dev`

When a model has a knowledge base attached, `GET /api/models` inlines the
fully-extracted text of every knowledge file into the response, under

single model with a moderately large knowledge base can add tens of MB to the
response, which times out or breaks tools that consume the model list. The
model list never uses these bodies - the frontend renders knowledge badges

### Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced from source on the `dev` branch (v0.10.2), Python 3.11, SQLite,
no external provider configured.

   - `cd backend && uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -r requirements.txt`
   - `export WEBUI_SECRET_KEY="repro-secret-please-change"`
   - `bash dev.sh`  (uvicorn on http://localhost:8080; wait for "Application startup complete.")

2. Create the first user (becomes admin) and grab a token:
   - `TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/auths/signup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Admin","email":"admin@example.com","password":"reproPassword123"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])')`

3. Provide one base model so the model list is non-empty (a clean instance with
   no OpenAI/Ollama provider otherwise returns an empty list). Create a minimal
   pipe function and activate it:
   - `curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/functions/create -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"id":"reprobase","name":"reprobase","content":"class Pipe:\n    def __init__(self):\n        pass\n    def pipe(self, body: dict):\n        return \"ok\"\n","meta":{"description":"repro base"}}'`
   - `curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/v1/functions/id/reprobase/toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`

4. Create a preset model with an attached knowledge base of 20 files, each
   carrying ~2 MB of extracted text (this is exactly the shape the frontend
   persists when you attach knowledge in the model editor):
   - Use the script below (builds the payload and prints the response size).

5. Call `GET /api/models` and observe the size:
   - `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" localhost:8080/api/models | wc -c`

Reproduction script (steps 2-5 in one file):

    # repro.py - run: python3 repro.py
    import json, urllib.request
    BASE="http://localhost:8080"
    def req(m,p,tok=None,body=None):
        r=urllib.request.Request(BASE+p,data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None,method=m)
        r.add_header("Content-Type","application/json")
        if tok: r.add_header("Authorization",f"Bearer {tok}")
        try: return urllib.request.urlopen(r).read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.read()
    tok=json.loads(req("POST","/api/v1/auths/signin",body={"email":"admin@example.com","password":"reproPassword123"}))["token"]
    req("POST","/api/v1/functions/create",tok,{"id":"reprobase","name":"reprobase","content":"class Pipe:\n    def pipe(self, body: dict):\n        return 'ok'\n","meta":{}})
    req("POST","/api/v1/functions/id/reprobase/toggle",tok)
    content="lorem ipsum "*(2_000_000//12)
    kb=[{"id":f"file-{i}","name":f"doc_{i}.txt","type":"file","data":{"content":content}} for i in range(20)]
    req("POST","/api/v1/models/create",tok,{"id":"repro-rag","name":"repro-rag","base_model_id":"reprobase","meta":{"knowledge":kb},"params":{}})
    resp=req("GET","/api/models?refresh=true",tok)
    print("GET /api/models total bytes:",len(resp))

Not applicable: this is a backend response-serialization issue reproduced from
source (uvicorn), so there are no browser console logs or Docker container logs.
Diagnostic evidence is the response size measured on identical data (20 files
× ~2 MB extracted text each) on the `dev` branch:

| GET /api/models          | bytes        |
|--------------------------|-------------:|
| total response           | 40,002,222 B |
| the model's entry        | 40,001,991 B |
| knowledge data.content   | present      |

The `repro-rag` entry alone is ~40 MB - driven entirely by
`info.meta.knowledge[*].data.content`.


### Additional Information

Same "don't materialize `data.content` unless requested" concern as #26144
(knowledge files endpoint) and the precedent in #25774 (`content: bool` query
param on the files endpoints) - this issue covers the `/api/models` path, which
neither of those addresses.

title: feat: Per-model / per-connection default-enable for external (OpenAPI) tool servers
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched existing open **and closed** issues/discussions. Closest matches are all closed without covering this case: #17596 (closed "completed"), #14632, #18392.

### Problem Description

External OpenAPI tool servers (Settings → Integrations → Manage Tool Servers) can only be toggled **per chat**. Every new chat resets them to *off*, and there is no per-model or per-connection "enabled by default" option:

- The **connection dialog → Advanced** only configures the OpenAPI spec path - there's no "enable by default" flag.
- The **Model Editor → Tools** (`toolIds`) default-enable list only covers **Workspace** tools, not external tool-server tools.

As a result, anyone relying on an OpenAPI tool server (e.g. a private RAG or web-search backend) has to manually enable it in **every** new chat. Worse, until it's toggled on, the model falls back to the built-in `search_notes` / `search_memories` / `query_knowledge_files` toolkits, which shadow the external tool and return empty results - so the out-of-the-box experience looks broken.

Note: #17596 ("Default enabled external tools server") was closed as *completed*, but on v0.10.2 there is no per-connection default-enable toggle for **user-added** tool servers, so that fix (if any) appears limited to admin/global servers.

### Desired Solution

Either (or both) of:

1. An **"Enabled by default"** toggle on each tool-server connection (Settings → Integrations), so its tools are active in new chats without manual toggling.
2. Allow **external tool-server tools to be selected in the Model Editor's default tools** (`toolIds`), exactly like Workspace tools - so a model preset can pre-enable them and (optionally) suppress the competing built-in toolkits.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Re-implementing the tool as a Workspace (Python) tool** - works and *is* selectable as a model default, but it duplicates the tool logic inside Open WebUI and forfeits the benefits of a standard external OpenAPI server (independent lifecycle, reuse by other clients).
- **`TOOL_SERVER_CONNECTIONS` env var** - applies to global servers and concerns persistence, not per-model auto-enable.

### Additional Context

Open WebUI v0.10.2. Use case: a self-hosted LLM served via vLLM with native tool-calling, plus a private OpenAPI tool server exposing web-search and semantic (RAG) search. Tool-calling works perfectly once the server is toggled on - the only gap is that it can't be made default-on per model.

title: issue: deprecated authlib.jose import warns on startup and breaks the OIDC stale-JWKS retry (wrong BadSignatureError class)
body:
## Describe the bug

Every backend startup logs a deprecation warning:

```
/app/backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py:19: AuthlibDeprecationWarning: authlib.jose module is deprecated, please use joserfc instead.
It will be compatible before version 2.0.0.
  from authlib.jose.errors import BadSignatureError
```

Beyond the log noise, the deprecated import hides a functional bug: `handle_callback` in `backend/open_webui/utils/oauth.py` catches `authlib.jose.errors.BadSignatureError` to evict a stale cached JWKS and retry when an IdP rotates its signing keys. Since Authlib 1.7, the OIDC client decodes ID tokens via **joserfc** and raises `joserfc.errors.BadSignatureError` - a class with a completely disjoint hierarchy - so the recovery path can never trigger. A rotated signing key with a reused `kid` fails the login with `INVALID_CRED` instead of refreshing the JWKS and retrying.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the backend (`ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:dev`) and watch the startup logs - the `AuthlibDeprecationWarning` is printed.
2. (Recovery-path bug) With an OIDC provider configured, rotate the IdP signing key while keeping the same `kid`, then attempt a login with the stale JWKS cached - the login fails with `INVALID_CRED` instead of refetching the key set.

## Expected behavior

No deprecation warning on startup; the bad-signature JWKS-eviction retry actually catches the exception Authlib ≥1.7 raises (`joserfc.errors.BadSignatureError`).

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` image (`authlib==1.7.2`, `joserfc` 1.7.4 installed transitively but not declared in requirements)

## Additional context

- `joserfc` is already imported directly by `oauth.py` (`JWSRegistry`, `HeaderParameter`) but is not declared in `requirements.txt` / `requirements-min.txt` / `pyproject.toml`.
- I have a small fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: admin Analytics settings tab expands outside the settings modal
body:
## Describe the bug

On the latest `dev` branch, the admin **Settings → Analytics** tab can expand outside the settings modal: the Model Usage / User Activity tables and chart render past the modal's right edge (columns clipped against the page background, no horizontal scrolling), instead of being contained within the modal.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the `dev` image with a sizable analytics history (e.g. years of data) and open **Settings → Analytics** as an admin.
2. Select **All time**.
3. On viewports where the modal's content area is narrower than the tab's intrinsic content width (readily reproducible below ~1350px effective viewport width), the tab's content column blows out past the modal boundary.

## Expected behavior

The Analytics tab should stay inside the settings modal at every viewport width, with the usage tables scrolling horizontally inside their own containers when space is tight.

## Additional context

Two containment gaps combine here:

1. The settings content column in `SettingsModal.svelte` is a `flex-1` item of the modal's `md:flex-row` without `min-w-0`, so its automatic minimum size is its min-content width - wide tab content pushes the whole column out of the modal.
2. `ChartLine.svelte`'s SVG (`viewBox="0 0 1000 ..."`, `w-full`) sits in normal flow inside its fixed-height container; a viewBox gives the SVG an intrinsic aspect ratio, so with a definite height it contributes ~1000px of min-content width to every ancestor even though `preserveAspectRatio="none"` means the ratio is visually meaningless.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: bug: Native tool calling drops final answer content after 2+ rounds of tool calls
body:
## Bug: Native tool calling - final answer content silently dropped after 2+ rounds of tool calls

### Environment
- Open WebUI version: v0.10.2
- Backend: OpenAI-compatible connection to `mlx_lm.server` (MLX, Apple Silicon), model `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit`
- Model config: `function_calling: native`, one custom tool attached (via `tool_ids`)
- Reproduced consistently across multiple prompts and multiple tool functions (both a custom third-party tool and Open WebUI's own built-in Knowledge-RAG tool)

### Summary
When native tool calling requires **two or more sequential tool calls** before the model can answer (e.g. "look up X" → "now use X to look up Y" → answer), the final assistant message is sometimes stored/returned as **completely empty** (`content: ""`, `finish_reason: "stop"`), even though the underlying model generated a full, correct, complete answer.

### Root cause isolated
Using a logging reverse-proxy placed directly between Open WebUI and the inference backend, I captured the exact request/response for the final completion call (the one made after both tool calls resolved). The raw SSE stream from the backend contained a complete, coherent, correct 779-character answer, streamed token-by-token, ending with `finish_reason: "stop"`. This is the ground truth - the model and the serving backend behaved correctly.

However, the message that ends up in the chat's stored history (visible via the `chat:outlet` socket event, and to the end user) has `content: ""`. Something in Open WebUI's own aggregation of the streamed response across the multi-round native tool-calling loop is failing to carry that final content through.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a model with `function_calling: native` and attach a tool whose typical use requires the model to make 2+ sequential tool calls to answer a question (e.g., a "look up an ID" tool followed by a "look up details by ID" tool).
2. Ask a question that requires this multi-step lookup.
3. Observe: the tool calls execute correctly (visible in the UI as separate tool-call cards, with real correct arguments and real correct tool output), but the final assistant message is blank.
4. Not deterministic - the same exact prompt against the same exact tool call sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.

### Expected behavior
The model's final generated content should reliably reach the stored chat message and the user, regardless of how many tool-call rounds preceded it.

### Additional notes
- Not reproducible under `function_calling: legacy` - that code path works reliably.
- Checked existing issues; found related-but-not-identical closed reports involving native tool calling + streaming content loss for other providers (Gemini, vLLM reasoning_content), but nothing matching this exact "empty final content after 2+ tool-call rounds" symptom for an OpenAI-compatible backend.
- Happy to provide the captured wire-level request/response logs (SSE dumps) if useful for debugging.

title: Errors in tool-call/code-interpreter continuation rounds are silently swallowed (empty assistant message, no error shown)
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- I have searched the existing issues and discussions and found no report of this bug.

### Installation Method

Docker (official image, `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui`)

### Open WebUI Version

v0.10.2 (the affected code is unchanged on current `dev`)

### Ollama Version (if applicable)

n/a (OpenAI-compatible backend behind a proxy)

### Operating System

Linux (containerized, AWS ECS)

### Browser (if applicable)

n/a (server-side bug; verified via chat DB and backend logs)

### Expected Behavior

When the model requests native tool calls and the follow-up model invocation (the "continuation" round that synthesizes the final answer from the tool results) fails - e.g. the upstream endpoint returns HTTP 400 - the user should see an error message on the chat message, and the error should be recorded on the message in the DB, like other error paths in `streaming_chat_response_handler` already do (e.g. the tool-call iteration limit emits `chat:message:error` and persists an `error` field).

### Actual Behavior

The chat ends with a **silently empty assistant message**: `content=''`, `done=true`, and a final output item `{type: "message", status: "completed", text: ""}`. No error event reaches the frontend, no `error` field is persisted, and nothing is logged unless `GLOBAL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` is set.

Cause: in `backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py` (`streaming_chat_response_handler`), the native tool-call continuation loop wraps `generate_chat_completion` / `stream_body_handler` in:

```python
except Exception as e:
    log.debug(e)
    break
```

so **any** exception in a continuation round (round ≥ 2) is swallowed. The code-interpreter continuation a bit further down has the same pattern. On current `dev` these are the `except` blocks around lines ~5133 and ~5336.

Round-1 text (produced before the tool calls) survives, which makes the failure look like the model "answered with nothing" - with no diagnostic trail.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible connection through a proxy that can reject a request (in our case: LiteLLM with an AWS Bedrock guardrail that returned HTTP 400 "Violated guardrail policy" for the continuation request, because the raw web-search tool results in the round-2 payload triggered its prompt-attack filter).
2. Enable native function calling and a tool (e.g. built-in web search), ask a question that triggers tool use.
3. Round 1 streams fine and executes the tools; the round-2 request is rejected by the proxy (any 4xx/5xx or transient network error in that round reproduces it - the guardrail is just one way to trigger it).
4. The chat shows the round-1 text (if any) and then an empty final message; no error is displayed. The DB has `content=''` with `done=true`.

### Logs & Screenshots

With default log levels there is nothing in the log (that is the bug). With `GLOBAL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` the swallowed exception (the proxy's 400) appears via `log.debug(e)` at the location above. Verified against the model provider's invocation logs: the upstream model had fully streamed the round-2 answer; the rejection happened at the proxy layer, and open-webui dropped it silently.

### Additional Information

The fix is small and mirrors the existing iteration-limit error path in the same function (persist `{'error': {'content': ...}}` + emit `chat:message:error` + `log.exception`). PR follows.

### Expected Behavior

When using Temporary Chat mode with a model that has `builtin_tools: true` and the Task Management category enabled, either:
1. Task management tools (`create_tasks`/`update_task`) work with in-memory task storage for the session duration, OR
2. Task management tools are NOT injected in Temporary Chat mode, preventing the model from calling a tool that cannot succeed

### Actual Behavior

In Temporary Chat mode:
1. The model calls `create_tasks`. The task widget appears in the UI showing N tasks
2. When the model calls `update_task` with a task ID, it returns: `{"error": "Task with id \"1\" not found"}`
3. The task widget remains stuck at **0/N tasks completed** and never updates
4. The model detects the failure and falls back: "It seems there's an issue with the task management system. Let me try a different approach..."

In regular (persistent) chats, task management works correctly end-to-end.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy Open WebUI v0.10.2 with the following environment variables:
   ```
   DEFAULT_MODEL_PARAMS='{"function_calling": "native"}'
   DEFAULT_MODEL_METADATA='{"capabilities": {"builtin_tools": true}}'
   ```
2. Connect to an OpenAI-compatible backend that supports native tool calling (tested with Claude via AWS Bedrock, but any model with function calling support will reproduce this)
3. Open the Open WebUI chat interface in Chrome
4. Click the **Temporary Chat** toggle in the top bar (the icon with a clock/timer - it turns blue when active)
5. Select any model (tested with Claude Sonnet 4 and Claude Haiku 4.5 via OpenAI-compatible API)
6. Ensure the model has **Capabilities → Builtin Tools → Task Management** enabled (this is the default when `builtin_tools: true`)
7. Send this prompt: "Research the pros and cons of microservices vs monoliths, then give a recommendation for a team of 5"
8. Observe: the model calls `create_tasks`, the task widget appears with 3-5 tasks
9. Observe: the model then calls `update_task` with `{"id": "1", "status": "completed"}`
10. **Result:** The tool returns `{"error": "Task with id \"1\" not found"}`. The widget stays at 0/N

**Contrast with regular chat:** Disable Temporary Chat, send the same prompt. Tasks are created and updated correctly, widget shows progress.

### Logs & Screenshots

### Tool call output (visible by expanding the tool call detail in the UI):

**create_tasks - succeeds (partially):**
```
INPUT:
{
  "tasks": [
    {"content": "Research pros and cons of microservices architecture", "status": "pending"},
    {"content": "Research pros and cons of monolithic architecture", "status": "pending"},
    {"content": "Compare scalability, maintainability, deployment, team dynamics", "status": "pending"},
    {"content": "Provide recommendation for a team of 5", "status": "pending"}
  ]
}

OUTPUT:
(task widget appears showing 0/4 tasks completed)
```

**update_task - fails:**
```
INPUT:
{
  "id": "1",
  "status": "completed"
}

OUTPUT:
{
  "error": "Task with id \"1\" not found"
}
```

### Additional Information

### Root cause (from source inspection):

The task management tool stores tasks in the `chats` database table (`tasks` JSON column) via `Chats.update_chat_tasks_by_id(chat_id, tasks)` in `backend/open_webui/models/chats.py`. In Temporary Chat mode, the `__chat_id__` passed to the tool is either `None` or a transient identifier that does not exist in the `Chat` table, so the DB write silently fails and subsequent reads return nothing.

title: Preset terminal selection is silently lost when terminal discovery resolves after chat defaults/mount
body:
## Environment

- Open WebUI: `v0.10.2`
- Build/source commit: `ecd48e2f718220a6400ecf49eafd4867a38feb10`
- Affected source areas at that commit:
  - `src/lib/components/chat/Chat.svelte:393-399,503-509` (`isTerminalAvailable` / preset application)
  - `src/lib/components/chat/Chat.svelte:934-948` (mount-time stale selection cleanup)
  - `src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte:174-185,217-218` (asynchronous terminal loading)

## Summary

A model preset can provide a valid `meta.terminalId`, but the selection is evaluated before the asynchronously loaded terminal inventory is available. `setDefaults()` then treats the terminal as unavailable and does not select it. When a persisted selection is restored during a hard reload, the mount-time stale check can also clear it while the terminal store is still empty. Arrival of the terminal list does not retry the preset or restore the cleared selection.

This makes a valid preset timing-dependent. It can require a manual terminal selection even though the configured terminal becomes available shortly afterward.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Configure a visible model preset with terminal capability enabled and a valid `meta.terminalId`.
2. Start Open WebUI with that terminal available from the system-terminal endpoint, but delay the terminal-list response so chat defaults/mount run first.
3. Open a new chat with the preset, or hard-reload a chat after persisting the same terminal ID in `localStorage.selectedTerminalId`.
4. Let terminal discovery resolve.
5. Observe the selected terminal and persisted terminal ID.

A deterministic schedule reproducing the source semantics:

### Availability race

- `20 ms`: `setDefaults()` receives `terminal-builder`; terminal inventory is still empty, so it is considered unavailable.
- `120 ms`: terminal inventory resolves with `terminal-builder`.
- Final state: no selected terminal and no persisted terminal ID, despite the terminal now being available.

### Mount-time stale clear

- `0 ms`: restore `terminal-builder` from local storage.
- `10 ms`: mount-time stale check runs against the still-empty terminal inventory and clears the selection.
- `100 ms`: terminal inventory resolves with `terminal-builder`.
- Final state: no selected terminal and no persisted terminal ID.

## Expected behavior

A valid preset or persisted terminal selection should survive asynchronous terminal discovery. Once discovery has completed, Open WebUI should select the requested terminal if it is available. A genuinely stale terminal ID should still be cleared after the inventory is authoritative.

## Actual behavior

The requested terminal is silently discarded while the inventory is temporarily empty. The later terminal-list update does not trigger another preset/selection check.

## Why this is a race rather than an invalid preset

The same terminal ID is present in the resolved inventory. Only event ordering changes the outcome. Local deterministic source-semantics tests reproduce both failure schedules without DOM automation, polling, or network mutation.

The deterministic downstream evidence consists of a machine-readable timing trace, a source-semantics harness, and regression tests. I can provide the harness and raw output if useful.

## Suggested direction (not a complete PR design)

Please coordinate preset application and stale cleanup with completion of terminal discovery:

1. Treat an empty/not-yet-loaded terminal store as **unknown**, not as proof that the requested ID is stale.
2. After the terminal inventory has loaded successfully, re-evaluate the pending preset/persisted terminal ID once.
3. Clear a persisted terminal ID only after discovery is authoritative and confirms that the ID is absent.
4. Preserve explicit user changes made while loading; the retry must not overwrite a different terminal selected by the user.
5. Do not solve this with DOM clicks or periodic polling.

One possible implementation is to retain a pending requested terminal ID and consume it when terminal loading reaches a completed state, guarded by "selection unchanged since request". Alternatively, await terminal loading before the initial defaults/stale-cleanup pass. The important contract is that a temporary empty store is not treated as final availability evidence.

## Acceptance checks

- Preset ID exists, inventory resolves later → preset terminal is selected exactly once.
- Persisted ID exists, inventory resolves later → selection is not cleared prematurely.
- ID is absent after successful inventory load → stale selection is cleared.
- User selects another terminal while discovery is pending → late retry does not overwrite it.
- Terminal request fails → no forced selection and no destructive stale clear based only on the failed/unknown inventory.
- No DOM click simulation or polling loop.

## Evidence boundary

The downstream reproduction is deterministic and models the exact v0.10.2 source ordering. It is not claimed as a production browser timing capture: no live Open WebUI mutation, browser smoke, API credential use, or upstream publication was performed while preparing this draft.

title: issue: Claude reasoning signature still not persisted, get_reasoning_details prefers the unsigned top-level reasoning_details over the signed provider_specific_fields copy so every prior thinking block is dropped on replay
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues.
- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions.
- [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items that resolve this.
- [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI (v0.10.2).

**Related prior reports** (this issue consolidates them and adds concrete evidence on the current code path):
- Discussion #18077 (2025-10-06) - same root cause via Bedrock, reported with a proposed fix in the author's fork. **0 replies, never triaged.**
- #23339 (open since 2026-04-02, 43 comments) - requests a toggle to disable reinjecting reasoning; describes the same `convert_output_to_messages(..., raw=True)` reinjection mechanism, but frames the symptom as `<think>`-tag imitation rather than a hard API rejection.
- #19328 (closed 2026-01-09) - fixed `reasoning_details` preservation across **tool steps** only; the plain multi-turn persistence path still drops the signature.

### Installation Method
Docker

### Open WebUI Version
v0.10.2

### Operating System
macOS (Docker)

### Bug Description

**Open WebUI receives Anthropic's `thinking` block signature and discards it when persisting the assistant message. On the next turn it reinjects the reasoning rebuilt from storage - without the signature - and the provider rejects the entire request.**

The result is that **any multi-turn conversation with a reasoning-enabled Claude model dies permanently on its second message**:

```
messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block
```

The affected conversation cannot recover - every subsequent turn fails the same way, and the block cannot be repaired from the UI. Starting a new chat works until *it* reaches turn 2.

This is not provider flakiness: OpenRouter retried across **five** providers (Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock ×2, Google Vertex, Azure) and all five returned the identical 400, which is expected because the outgoing payload is malformed before it leaves.

### Evidence - live response vs. what gets stored

Captured on the same model (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` via OpenRouter) on v0.10.2. Signature value redacted; only its presence and length are shown.

**What arrives from the provider** (`choices[0].message.provider_specific_fields.reasoning_details[0]`):

```json
{
  "type": "reasoning.text",
  "text": "...",
  "format": "anthropic-claude-v1",
  "index": 0,
  "signature": "<~1872 chars, redacted>"
}
```

**What Open WebUI stores** (`chat.history.messages[<assistant-id>].output[].reasoning_details[0]` in `webui.db`):

```json
{
  "type": "reasoning.text",
  "text": "...",
  "format": "anthropic-claude-v1",
  "index": 0
}
```

`signature` is **absent**. Searching the entire stored chat record for the string `signature` returns matches only inside the *saved error text* of the failed turn - never in the reasoning data itself.

The assistant message is stored with `content: ""` and the reasoning under `output[] → {"type": "reasoning", "reasoning_details": [...]}`.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Configure a Claude model with reasoning enabled (reproduced via OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`; discussion #18077 reports the same via Bedrock).
2. Send any message that causes the model to produce a reasoning block.
3. Send a **second** message in the same conversation.
4. The request fails with `messages.1.content.0: Invalid \`signature\` in \`thinking\` block`.

Independent confirmation that the stored shape is the trigger - posting the stored shape directly to the provider reproduces it deterministically:

```json
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi!",
 "reasoning_details": [{"type": "reasoning.text", "text": "...",
                        "format": "anthropic-claude-v1", "index": 0}]}
```

→ same 400. Re-adding a valid `signature` to that entry makes it succeed.

### Expected Behavior

Either:
1. **Persist `signature`** in `reasoning_details` so reinjected reasoning validates (preferred - preserves cross-turn reasoning continuity); **or**
2. **Do not reinject** prior-turn reasoning that lacks a signature. Anthropic explicitly permits omitting it outside tool use - from their thinking docs: *Required:* within a tool-use turn, pass thinking blocks back; *Recommended:* across turns; **Allowed:** outside tool use, omit prior turns' thinking.

Option 2 is what #23339 requests as a toggle.

Note that (1) and (2) are not equivalent for existing data: because the signature was never written, **already-stored conversations cannot be repaired** - only (2) rescues them.

### Actual Behavior

The signature is dropped at persistence time and the unverifiable reasoning block is reinjected on the next turn, producing a hard 400 that permanently breaks the conversation.

### Impact

Every reasoning-enabled Claude conversation is limited to a single turn. For non-technical users the failure is opaque - the chat simply stops working with a provider error, and the only workaround is to start a new chat, which then breaks the same way.

### Workaround (for anyone else hitting this)

If you front Open WebUI with a proxy (e.g. LiteLLM), strip `reasoning_details` entries that have no `signature` from **prior** assistant turns before the request goes upstream, leaving tool-use turns untouched. Reasoning stays fully enabled; only unverifiable *prior-turn* reasoning is omitted. Dropping only *unsigned* entries means the workaround becomes a no-op automatically once this is fixed upstream.

title: issue: sidebar chat row flickers between title truncation and timestamp while hovering
body:
## Describe the bug

Hovering a chat in the sidebar and moving the pointer horizontally makes the row flicker: the title repeatedly toggles between its full and truncated form, and the "time ago" label appears and disappears. At intermediate moments the timestamp is drawn underneath the action buttons, so both are visible on top of each other.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the sidebar so the chat list is visible.
2. Hover a chat row.
3. Without leaving the row, move the pointer side to side across it - for example between the title and the `···` button.
4. The title flips between `Some chat title` and `Some chat tit...`, the timestamp flashes in and out, and briefly overlaps the action buttons.

## Expected behavior

Hover state should be stable for as long as the pointer is anywhere on the row: the actions stay visible, the timestamp stays hidden, and the title keeps a constant width.

## Root cause

In `src/lib/components/layout/Sidebar/ChatItem.svelte`, one flag drives two layout-affecting decisions:

```js
$: showInlineActions = id === $chatId || confirmEdit || mouseOver || selected;
```

- the timestamp is only rendered when it is false - `{#if (updatedAt ?? createdAt) && !showInlineActions}`
- the title gets `pr-12` when it is true, which is what makes it truncate

The row container tracks hover correctly, but the action-menu container nested inside it also sets `mouseOver` from its own `on:mouseenter` / `on:mouseleave`. `mouseleave` fires whenever the pointer leaves that child element's box, even while the pointer is still inside the row, so moving off the `···` area sets `mouseOver = false`. The timestamp comes back and the title un-truncates, while the buttons remain on screen because their visibility also comes from the CSS `group-hover:visible` on the row - which is why both render at once.

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` branch
- Browser: any (hover/layout, not browser-specific)

## Additional context

A fix is ready and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: dropdowns in the Manage Models modal are inset from the right edge of their container
body:
## Describe the bug

Both dropdowns in the **Manage Models** modal stop about 6px short of the right edge of the box they sit in, so they look inset compared with the text inputs above and below them. It is easiest to see by focusing the *Delete a model* dropdown: the blue focus border ends before the grey container does, leaving a visible strip of background on the right.

The Ollama instance picker at the top of the modal has the same gap; it is just less noticeable because nothing sits beside it, so the select is short against its own container rather than against a neighbouring button.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open **Admin Settings → Models → Manage Models** (with Ollama configured).
2. Click the *Delete a model* dropdown, then click elsewhere so it keeps its focus ring.
3. The focus border stops short of the right edge of the grey box, and the dropdown does not line up with the *Pull a model* / *Create a model* inputs.
4. The same inset is present on the Ollama instance dropdown at the top of the modal.

## Root cause

`SettingsSelect` is self-contained - it renders its own background, border, rounding and `focus:border-blue-400` ring. In these two places it is wrapped in a legacy container that also paints a background *and* adds right padding:

- `src/lib/components/admin/Settings/Models/Manage/ManageMultipleOllama.svelte`
  `<div class="flex-1 mb-2.5 pr-1.5 rounded-lg bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-850">`
- `src/lib/components/admin/Settings/Models/Manage/ManageOllama.svelte`
  `<div class="flex-1 mr-2 pr-1.5 rounded-lg bg-gray-50 dark:bg-gray-850">`

The select's `w-full` fills the wrapper's content box, which `pr-1.5` has already shrunk by 6px. The sibling rows do not have this: *Pull a model* and *Create a model* put their `<input class="w-full ...">` straight into `<div class="flex-1 mr-2">`, which is why only the dropdowns look inset.

These are the only two `SettingsSelect` instances in the codebase wrapped in a background box, and the only two carrying that padding; every other `pr-1.5` in `src/lib` is a scrollbar gutter or an element's own padding.

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` branch
- Browser: any (CSS layout)

## Additional context

A fix is ready and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: browser Back button does not work after opening Admin Panel, Evaluations, or Workspace
body:
## Describe the bug

The browser's Back button does not work after navigating to any section that goes through an index route: the Admin Panel, the admin Evaluations tab, or Workspace. Pressing Back appears to do nothing - you stay on the same page.

## Steps to reproduce

1. From a chat, open the user menu and click **Admin Panel**. You land on `/admin/users/overview`.
2. Press the browser's Back button - you stay on `/admin/users/overview` instead of returning to the chat.

The same happens with:

- **Evaluations** in the admin panel (`/admin/evaluations/leaderboard`)
- **Workspace** in the sidebar (`/workspace/models`)

## Root cause

These are index routes whose only job is to forward, and they forward with a plain `goto()`, which *pushes* a history entry instead of replacing it. Clicking Admin Panel therefore stacks three entries:

```
[previous page] → /admin → /admin/users → /admin/users/overview
```

Back moves to `/admin/users`, whose `onMount` immediately forwards to `/admin/users/overview` again, so the user never escapes. `/workspace` → `/workspace/models` and `/admin/evaluations` → `/admin/evaluations/leaderboard` behave the same way with two entries.

The correct pattern is already used elsewhere in the codebase - `src/routes/(app)/admin/settings/+page.svelte` calls `goto(..., { replaceState: true })`, and `src/routes/(app)/admin/analytics/+page.svelte` uses it in one branch but not the other.

The same trap applies to the guard redirects in these trees: a user without permission is bounced from `/workspace/models` to `/`, and pressing Back returns them to the forbidden page only to be bounced again.

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` branch
- Browser: any

## Additional context

A fix is ready and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: deleting an Ollama API connection does not persist unless the Ollama API toggle is switched afterwards
body:
## Describe the bug

Deleting an Ollama API connection in **Admin Settings → Connections** does not persist. The connection disappears from the list, but leaving the Connections tab and returning brings it back, as if it was never deleted.

The deletion only sticks if you toggle the **Ollama API** switch off and back on *after* deleting.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Go to **Admin Settings → Connections** and add a second Ollama connection (any URL will do).
2. Delete it using the connection's delete action - it disappears from the list.
3. Navigate to another settings tab and back to **Connections** - the deleted connection is listed again.
4. Now delete it again and toggle **Ollama API** off and back on - this time it stays deleted.

## Root cause

In `src/lib/components/admin/Settings/Connections.svelte`, the Ollama connection's `onDelete` only mutates local component state - it filters `OLLAMA_BASE_URLS` and reindexes `OLLAMA_API_CONFIGS`, but never calls `updateOllamaHandler()`, so nothing is sent to the backend. Re-entering the tab re-fetches the stored config and the connection returns.

The OpenAI connection immediately above it does not have this problem: its `onDelete` ends with `updateOpenAIHandler()`.

The toggle workaround works because the `Ollama API` switch calls `updateOllamaHandler()` from its `on:change`, which persists the whole config - including the already-shortened URL list.

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` branch
- Browser: any

## Additional context

A fix is ready and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: moving an archived chat into a folder never unarchives it, and folder contents don't refresh after menu moves
body:
## Describe the bug

Moving an archived chat into a folder appears to do nothing. Two independent defects combine:

1. **The chat is never unarchived, so the move has no visible effect.** The move endpoint writes `folder_id` but leaves the chat archived, and folder listings only show unarchived chats - so the chat never appears in the folder. It remains visible in Settings → Archived Chats the whole time, exactly as before the move. The written `folder_id` is inert in the normal flow, too: individually unarchiving goes through `toggle_chat_archive_by_id`, which sets `folder_id = None`, so the chat returns to the main list rather than the folder. (The only code path that would preserve it is *Unarchive All*, whose bulk update flips `archived` without touching `folder_id`.)
2. **The sidebar does not refresh.** Moving *any* chat (archived or not) into a folder from the open chat's menu (chat title → Move) never refreshes an expanded folder's contents in the sidebar. Archiving a folder-resident chat from the same menu has the same problem - it stays visible in the folder until a reload.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Archive a chat, then open it (e.g. from Settings → Archived Chats).
2. Use the chat title menu → **Move** → pick a folder.
3. The move toasts success, but the chat does not appear in the folder - not even after a page reload - and it is still listed under Settings → Archived Chats (defect 1).
4. Separately: move a normal chat into an expanded folder using the same menu - the folder's contents do not update until it is collapsed and reopened or the page is reloaded (defect 2).

## Root cause

**Backend** - `Chats.update_chat_folder_id_by_id_and_user_id` normalizes `pinned = False` on move but leaves `archived` untouched, while `get_chats_by_folder_id_and_user_id` filters `archived=False`. The move therefore half-applies: `folder_id` is written, but the chat stays archived and the folder never lists it.

**Frontend** - the sidebar's folder contents live in per-folder component state, refreshed via a `folderRegistry` of callbacks that only `Sidebar.svelte` can reach. The sidebar-row menu's move routes through the sidebar (`dispatch('change') → initChatList → refreshChatRows`), which sweeps that registry - but the open chat's menu in `Chat.svelte` only calls the store-level `refreshChatList`, which refreshes the flat list and pinned chats, never the folders.

## Expected behavior

Moving a chat into a folder is an explicit organizational action: the chat should become visible in that folder immediately - unarchived if necessary, mirroring how the same method already un-pins on move - and expanded folders in the sidebar should reflect moves and archives right away.

## Environment

- Open WebUI: current `dev` branch

## Additional context

A fix is ready and I will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: sidebar folder chat list flashes/collapses when clicking a folder title
body:
## Bug Description

Clicking a folder's title in the sidebar causes a visible glitch in the folder tree: the chat list inside an expanded folder momentarily disappears (replaced by the loading dots) and then pops back in, looking like the folder collapses and re-expands. It happens when clicking either collapsed or expanded folder titles, and is most noticeable on expanded folders that have visible chats.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have at least one sidebar folder expanded with a few chats inside it.
2. Click the folder's title (not the chevron) - or the title of any other folder.
3. Watch the expanded folder's chat list: it briefly vanishes and re-appears.

## Expected Behavior

Selecting a folder should not visually disturb the folder tree. Expanded folders should keep their chat lists on screen; any background refresh should replace the list in place.

## Actual Behavior

The expanded folder's chat list is wiped from the DOM for a moment and then re-rendered, producing a collapse/re-expand flash.

## Root Cause

A single title click triggers a burst of overlapping `setFolderItems()` calls on every folder:

- The title click handler sets `selectedFolder` and navigates to `/folders/<id>`, whose `onMount` sets `selectedFolder` again.
- `Sidebar.svelte` has `$: if ($selectedFolder) initFolders();`, which rebuilds the `folders` object on each of those writes.
- `Folders.svelte` has `$: if (folders || ($selectedFolder && $chatId)) loadFolderItems();`, which re-runs on every change to `folders` or `$selectedFolder` and calls `setFolderItems()` on every registered folder.

In `RecursiveFolder.svelte`, `setFolderItems()` guards against concurrent fetches like this:

```js
if (open && !chatsLoading) {
	// fetch and replace `chats`
} else {
	chats = null; // reset state - intended for collapsed folders
	chatsPage = 1;
	hasMoreChats = false;
}
```

The `else` branch is meant to reset state when the folder is collapsed, but it also runs when the folder is **open and a fetch is already in flight** (`open && chatsLoading`). In the burst above, call A starts fetching, call B arrives while `chatsLoading` is still `true`, falls into the `else`, and sets `chats = null` - instantly emptying the visible chat list - without refetching anything. When call A's fetch resolves, the chats pop back in. That wipe-and-repopulate is the flash.

## Proposed Fix

Restrict the reset branch to folders that are actually collapsed (`} else {` → `} else if (!open) {`). A redundant refresh that arrives during an in-flight fetch then becomes a no-op: the visible list stays on screen and is replaced in place when the in-flight fetch lands (the `{#each}` is keyed by `chat.id`, so unchanged items don't re-render). Collapse still resets state, and first expand still shows the loading indicator. Data freshness is unchanged - the old `else` branch didn't refetch in that case either; it only wiped the list.

A PR with this one-line fix will be linked shortly.

## Environment

- **Open WebUI Version:** current `dev` branch
- **Browser:** Chrome (also reproducible logic-wise in any browser)

## Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of both the frontend and backend.
- [x] I have checked the browser console and server logs.
- [x] I have searched existing issues and discussions for duplicates.

title: issue: clicking a sidebar folder title fires duplicate folder refetches and chat-list sweeps
body:
## Bug Description

Clicking a folder title in the sidebar triggers a burst of redundant network requests: the folder is fetched twice, the entire folder tree (`GET /api/v1/folders/` + `GET /api/v1/folders/shared`) is refetched twice, and every expanded folder's chat list is refetched 3-4 times - all for a single selection where nothing on the server changed.

This is the request-traffic side of #27533 (which fixed the visual flash that this same burst caused; the redundant traffic itself was noted there as out of scope).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Expand a few sidebar folders that contain chats.
2. Open the browser's Network tab (filter XHR).
3. Click a folder's title once.
4. Observe duplicated requests: `GET /api/v1/folders/<id>` ×2, `GET /api/v1/folders/` ×2, `GET /api/v1/folders/shared` ×2, and `GET /api/v1/folders/<id>/shared/chats?page=1` ×3-4 per expanded folder.

## Expected Behavior

Selecting a folder should fetch each resource once: the selected folder, one folder-tree refresh, and one chat-list fetch per expanded folder.

## Root Cause

Two independent redundancies compound:

1. **The folder route refetches what the click handler just fetched.** The sidebar title click handler (`RecursiveFolder.svelte`) fetches the folder via `getFolderById`, sets `selectedFolder`, and navigates to `/folders/<id>`. The route's `onMount` then unconditionally fetches the same folder again and sets `selectedFolder` a second time. Each `selectedFolder` write triggers `Sidebar.svelte`'s `$: if ($selectedFolder) initFolders();`, so the whole folder tree (`getFolders` + `getSharedFolders`) is rebuilt twice.

2. **`Folders.svelte` sweeps once per trigger, and every trigger fires twice.** Its reactive statement

   ```js
   $: if (folders || ($selectedFolder && $chatId)) {
   	loadFolderItems();
   }
   ```

   re-runs on every change to `folders`, `$selectedFolder`, or `$chatId` (the condition itself is always true, since `folders` is a truthy object). The `$selectedFolder` dependency is redundant: every consequential `selectedFolder` write - selection or a folder rename from the folder page - also triggers the Sidebar reactive above, which rebuilds `folders`, which re-runs this same statement. So each selection produces duplicate `setFolderItems()` sweeps across all folders on top of the doubled `initFolders()`.

## Proposed Fix

Two minimal changes, preserving all existing refresh semantics:

1. In `/folders/[folderId]/+page.svelte`, skip the `getFolderById` + `selectedFolder.set` when `selectedFolder` already holds the folder for this route (the sidebar-click case). Direct URL loads and refreshes still take the full path, and if the click handler's fetch failed the store is unset, so the route's fetch still acts as the fallback.
2. In `Folders.svelte`, drop the redundant `$selectedFolder` dependency (`folders || ($selectedFolder && $chatId)` → `folders || $chatId`). Selection-driven sweeps still happen exactly once via the `folders` rebuild; chat-open refreshes keep their `$chatId` trigger; folder-page renames still propagate via `selectedFolder.set` → `initFolders()` → `folders` rebuild → sweep.

`Sidebar.svelte`'s `$: if ($selectedFolder) initFolders();` is deliberately left untouched: it is the only propagation path that updates the sidebar tree after a rename/icon change made from the folder page header (`FolderTitle.svelte` re-sets `selectedFolder` with the same id), so it cannot be removed or guarded on the folder id without breaking that flow.

Result per title click (verified by counting fetches): `getFolderById` ×1, `getFolders` ×1, `getSharedFolders` ×1, and one chat-list fetch per expanded folder.

A PR with this fix will be linked shortly.

title: issue: two sidebar chat hover previews can be open at once, stacked on top of each other
body:
## Bug Description

Two sidebar chat hover previews can end up open at the same time, one card stacked on top of the other. The stale preview belongs to a chat the pointer already left; it stays open while the newly hovered chat opens its own preview on top of it.

## Steps to Reproduce

It is timing/path sensitive, but reliably reproducible:

1. Hover a sidebar chat until its preview card opens (300 ms).
2. Move the pointer to the next chat row on a slightly diagonal path - downward and drifting toward the preview card (to the right).
3. Stop the pointer dead on the second row and wait ~300 ms.
4. The second chat's preview opens while the first chat's preview remains stuck open behind it.

## Expected Behavior

At most one chat hover preview is visible at any time; hovering a new chat replaces the previous preview.

## Actual Behavior

The previous preview can remain open behind the new preview, overlapped by the new one.

## Root Cause

Each `ChatItem` owns an independent `LinkPreview.Root` (bits-ui) with no shared state, so nothing in the app enforces a single-open invariant. The stale-open state itself comes from how bits-ui closes an open preview:

- Once the content is mounted and open, the trigger's `pointerleave` handler is a deliberate no-op (`bits-ui/dist/bits/link-preview/link-preview.svelte.js`, `onpointerleave`: it only closes when content is *not* mounted). Closing is fully delegated to the `SafePolygon` helper.
- `SafePolygon` (`bits-ui/dist/internal/safe-polygon.svelte.js`) records an exit point when the pointer leaves the trigger and from then on re-evaluates **only on `pointermove`**. The pointer is allowed to stay inside a grace wedge fanning from the exit point to the content card. With `side="right" align="center"`, the card is up to ~280 px tall and vertically centered on the row, so the wedge covers several neighboring rows once the path drifts toward the card.
- The only non-move fallback is a single `requestAnimationFrame` scheduled at leave time, which the first subsequent `pointermove` cancels and never reschedules. `SafePolygon` supports a `transitIntentTimeout` that would close after the pointer stops making progress, but `LinkPreview` constructs it without that option, and `LinkPreview.Root` does not expose it.

Net effect: leave row A on a diagonal path, stop on row B while still inside row A's grace wedge → no further `pointermove` → A's geometry check never runs again and A stays open. Row B's own preview opens 300 ms later → two stacked cards.

## Proposed Fix

Enforce the missing invariant at the app level in `ChatItem.svelte`: a module-context variable holds a close callback for the currently open preview; whenever any item's preview opens (hover or keyboard focus - every open path flows through the bound `open` state), it force-closes the previously registered one and registers itself. This closes the stale card the moment a new one opens, regardless of which bits-ui close path failed (pointer wedge, scrolling under a stationary cursor, list reorders).

Known limitation, noted for transparency: a *single* preview can still linger if the pointer stops on a non-chat element inside the grace wedge (e.g., a section label), because bits-ui's `transitIntentTimeout` escape hatch is not reachable through `LinkPreview.Root`. That is an upstream bits-ui exposure gap; the overlap reported here is fully prevented.

A PR with this fix will be linked shortly.

## Environment

- **Open WebUI Version:** current `dev` branch
- **Browser:** Firefox (reproduced), mechanism is browser-independent

- Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed,
- Include any files or environmental changes,
- Identify the expected and actual result at each stage,
- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

When the code execution tool is enabled (default engine: Pyodide) and a model invokes it with simple Python code like `print("test")`, the tool should execute the code in the browser via Pyodide and return the output:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "stdout": "test\n",
  "stderr": "",
  "result": "test"
}
```

### Actual Behavior

Every code execution attempt fails immediately with:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "Client session disconnected.",
  "result": ""
}
```

Note the misleading `status: "success"` - the tool-call wrapper completed, but the actual execution failed. The error "Client session disconnected" is returned to `stderr`.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with a clean Debian 12 host.
2. Install Docker and `docker-compose` (v1, compose file format 3.x).
3. Create the following `docker-compose.yml`:

   ```yaml
   services:
     open-webui:
       image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:latest
       container_name: open-webui
       restart: unless-stopped
       ports:
         - "8080:8080"
       volumes:
         - ./open-webui-data:/app/backend/data
       environment:
         - ENABLE_WEBSOCKET_SUPPORT=true
   ```

4. Run `docker-compose up -d`.
5. Wait for the container to become healthy (`curl http://localhost:8080/health` returns `{"status":true}`).
6. Open Chrome or Firefox and navigate to `http://localhost:8080`.
7. Log in / create an admin account.
8. Go to Admin Settings → Code Execution and confirm it is enabled with engine = `pyodide` (this is the default).
9. Start a new chat with any model. Send a message like: "Run this Python code: print('test')".
10. The model invokes the code execution tool. The tool result shows:

    ```
    INPUT
    code
    print("test")

    OUTPUT
    {
      "status": "success",
      "stdout": "",
      "stderr": "Client session disconnected.",
      "result": ""
    }
    ```

11. Check the Docker container logs: `docker logs open-webui 2>&1 | grep -A5 AssertionError`
12. Observe repeated `AssertionError` tracebacks from `websockets/legacy/protocol.py` (full traceback in Logs section below).

### Logs & Screenshots

### Docker container logs - session disconnect warnings

AssertionError
```

### Package versions inside the container

```
uvicorn                0.41.0  (pinned: uvicorn[standard]==0.41.0 in requirements.txt)
websockets             16.0   (transitive dep: google-genai, langsmith)
wsproto                1.3.2  (transitive dep: uvicorn[standard])
python-socketio        5.16.2
python-engineio        4.13.3
```

### Config DB (code execution settings)

```
code_execution.enable = true
code_execution.engine = "pyodide"
code_execution.jupyter.url = ""
code_execution.jupyter.auth = ""
```

### Browser console

The browser console shows the Socket.IO connection repeatedly disconnecting and reconnecting. No explicit JS errors are logged - the disconnection is detected server-side.

### Additional Information

### Root cause analysis

When the code execution engine is set to `pyodide` (the default), code is sent to the browser via a bidirectional Socket.IO event call and executed in-browser via Pyodide. The execution path is:

1. `open_webui/tools/builtin.py` → `execute_code()` calls `__event_call__()` with `{'type': 'execute:python', ...}`
2. `__event_call__` is provided by `open_webui/socket/main.py` → `get_event_caller()` → `__event_caller__()`
3. `__event_caller__` looks up the client's `session_id` in `SESSION_POOL`, then calls `sio.call('events', ..., to=session_id)`

The `websockets` v16.0 library has a bug in `legacy/protocol.py:_drain_helper()` (line 308):

```python
assert waiter is None or waiter.cancelled()
```

This assertion fails during keepalive ping cycles and data transfers, crashing uvicorn's WebSocket connection handler. Each crash triggers the `disconnect` handler in `socket/main.py`, which removes the session from `SESSION_POOL`. The next code execution attempt finds no session and returns `{'error': 'Client session disconnected.'}`.

### Why `websockets` 16.0 is installed

`websockets` is **not** pinned in Open WebUI's `requirements.txt`. It is pulled in as a transitive dependency of `google-genai` and `langsmith`. The `uvicorn[standard]` extra also depends on `websockets` but does not pin a specific version. When both `websockets` and `wsproto` are installed, uvicorn defaults to `websockets` (its `ws` config defaults to `"auto"`, which prefers `websockets`).

### Future risk

The `websockets` library's `legacy` module was **removed entirely** in v17.0. If `websockets` is upgraded further (e.g., by a dependency update), the `AssertionError` tracebacks will become `ImportError` - making this a ticking time bomb.

### Suggested fixes

**Option 1 (Recommended): Force `wsproto` as the WebSocket implementation**

`wsproto` is already installed in the image (via `uvicorn[standard]`) and does not have this bug. Add `--ws wsproto` to the uvicorn startup command in `start.sh`:

```bash
exec env WEBUI_SECRET_KEY="${WEBUI_SECRET_KEY:-}" \
  "$PYTHON_CMD" -m uvicorn open_webui.main:app \
    --host "$HOST" \
    --port "$PORT" \
    --forwarded-allow-ips "${FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS:-*}" \
    --ws wsproto \
    "${ARGS[@]}"
```

This is the least invasive fix and does not require pinning or downgrading any packages. Verified working: after applying this fix, the container starts cleanly with no `AssertionError` tracebacks and the code execution tool works correctly.

**Option 2: Pin `websockets` to a version without the bug**

Add to `requirements.txt`:

```
websockets<16.0
```

More fragile - may conflict with other dependencies that require `websockets>=16.0`.

**Option 3: Expose a `UVICORN_WS` environment variable**

Add a `UVICORN_WS` env var (defaulting to `wsproto`) so users can override the WebSocket implementation without modifying the startup script.

### Additional note on misleading status

The tool wrapper reports `"status": "success"` even when execution fails, because the tool-call plumbing completed - the error is only in `stderr`. This makes the issue especially confusing to debug. Consider checking whether `stderr` contains an error and reporting `status: "error"` in that case.

body:

- Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed,
- Include any files or environmental changes,
- Identify the expected and actual result at each stage,
- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

When uploading a PDF with Docling's `picture_description_api` configured (a nested JSON object) and `do_picture_description: true` (a boolean) set in the Docling **Parameters** field, Open WebUI should forward these values to `docling-serve` as valid JSON strings per its multipart form field, exactly as they are entered in the Parameters UI. The PDF should be processed successfully, with picture descriptions generated by the configured external VLM (e.g. via Ollama) and embedded in the resulting Markdown.

This exact same configuration, when sent directly to `docling-serve` via `curl` (bypassing Open WebUI), works correctly and produces the expected result.

### Actual Behavior

The upload consistently fails. The user-facing error (visible via the SSE stream in the browser Network tab) is generic:


{"status": "failed", "error": "Error calling Docling: Error calling Docling API: Internal Server Error - Internal Server Error"}


The `docling-serve` container logs reveal the real cause - a JSON validation error where the value received for the `picture_description_api` form field is not valid JSON at all. It looks like an arbitrary fragment of a Python dict's string representation (the exact fragment varies between runs - observed values include `'params'`, `'timeout'`, and `'classification_min_confidence'`):


ValueError: Invalid JSON for field 'picture_description_api': 1 validation error for nullable[PictureDescriptionApi]
Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1 [type=json_invalid, input_value='params', input_type=str]


Root cause identified in `open_webui/retrieval/loaders/main.py`, in `DoclingLoader.load()`:

```python
r = requests.post(
    f'{self.url}/v1/convert/file',
    files={
        'files': (
            self.file_path,
            f,
            self.mime_type or 'application/octet-stream',
        )
    },
    data={
        'image_export_mode': 'placeholder',
        'md_page_break_placeholder': page_break_marker,
        **self.params,
    },
    headers=headers,
    verify=AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SESSION_SSL,
)

self.params is a Python dict parsed from the user-configured DOCLING_PARAMS JSON. When **self.params is expanded directly into the data= dict passed to requests.post, any value that is itself a dict, list, or bool is NOT JSON-serialized by the requests library (it only knows how to encode primitive-like values for multipart form fields). This results in a broken/invalid string being sent for that field instead of a proper JSON string, which then fails Pydantic's validate_json() on the docling-serve side.

This affects any Docling Parameters option that isn't a flat string/number - not just picture_description_api, but also do_picture_description (a bool), and presumably other nested options such as VLM pipeline or table structure configs.

Suggested fix - JSON-encode non-primitive values before building the data dict:

data={
    'image_export_mode': 'placeholder',
    'md_page_break_placeholder': page_break_marker,
    **{
        k: (json.dumps(v) if isinstance(v, (dict, list, bool)) else v)
        for k, v in self.params.items()
    },
},

(json is already imported at the top of this file.)

We verified this fix locally by patching the file inside the running container and restarting Open WebUI - after the patch, the exact same Parameters configuration that failed before now works correctly end-to-end (PDF upload → Docling conversion → Ollama VLM call → picture descriptions correctly embedded in the resulting Markdown).

### Steps to Reproduce

## Steps to Reproduce
```markdown
1. Set up the following environment:
   - Open WebUI `v0.10.2`, running as a Docker container (`ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main`), port `3000:8080`.
   - `docling-serve` `1.27.0`, running as a separate Docker container (`ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-serve:main`), port `5001:5001`, on the same custom Docker bridge network as Open WebUI (e.g. `docker network create docling-net`, both containers attached via `--network docling-net`).
   - `docling-serve` started with the following environment variables:
     ```
     DOCLING_SERVE_ARTIFACTS_PATH=/opt/app-root/src/.cache/docling/models
     DOCLING_SERVE_ENABLE_REMOTE_SERVICES=true
     ```
   - Ollama running natively on the host machine (macOS, not in Docker), reachable from the `docling-serve` container via `http://host.docker.internal:11434`. Model `qwen2.5vl:7b` pulled and available (`ollama pull qwen2.5vl:7b`).

2. In Open WebUI, go to **Admin Panel > Settings > Documents**.

3. Set **Content Extraction Engine** to `Docling`, with the base URL `http://docling-serve:5001` (resolved via the shared Docker network).

4. In the **Parameters** field, enter the following JSON:
   ```json
   {
     "do_picture_description": true,
     "picture_description_api": {
       "url": "http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1/chat/completions",
       "params": { "model": "qwen2.5vl:7b" },
       "timeout": 120,
       "prompt": "Describe this image in Japanese, focusing on any graphs, charts, or diagrams."
     }
   }

Save the settings.

5. Go to the chat interface, attach/upload any PDF file that contains at least one image or figure (e.g. an academic paper with figures).

6. Observe that the upload fails. In the browser DevTools Network tab, the SSE response for the upload request shows:

data: {"status": "pending"}
data: {"status": "failed", "error": "Error calling Docling: Error calling Docling API: Internal Server Error - Internal Server Error"}

7. Check docker logs open-webui - it shows the exception originating from DoclingLoader.load() in open_webui/retrieval/loaders/main.py, raised from Error calling Docling API: Internal Server Error - Internal Server Error.

8. Check docker logs docling-serve - it shows the actual root-cause exception:

ValueError: Invalid JSON for field 'picture_description_api': 1 validation error for nullable[PictureDescriptionApi]
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1 [type=json_invalid, input_value='params', input_type=str]

9. As a control test, send the exact same payload directly to docling-serve, bypassing Open WebUI entirely:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/v1/convert/file \
  -F "files=@sample.pdf" \
  -F 'picture_description_api={"url":"http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1/chat/completions","params":{"model":"qwen2.5vl:7b"},"timeout":120,"prompt":"Describe this image in Japanese."}' \
  -F "do_picture_description=true"

This succeeds and returns a 200 response with picture descriptions correctly embedded in the resulting Markdown - confirming docling-serve itself works correctly, and the bug is isolated to how Open WebUI serializes and forwards the Parameters JSON.

### Logs & Screenshots

## Logs & Screenshots
```markdown

pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for nullable[PictureDescriptionApi]
Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1 [type=json_invalid, input_value='params', input_type=str]
For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/json_invalid
...

raise ValueError(f"Invalid JSON for field '{field_name}': {e}")
