title: enhancement: rows and controls repaint their parent surface's exact color, blocking instance theming (Redundant background repaints)
body:
## Summary

Thirteen spots across eleven frontend files hardcode `bg-white dark:bg-gray-900` (or, in the connection-server modals, a `dark:bg-gray-900` repaint inside the shared `selectClass` constant) on elements whose parent surface already paints exactly that color. In stock light and dark themes these classes are visually inert - each element repaints the pixel color it already sits on. Under instance theming (admin-injected custom CSS), however, they leave opaque boxes that refuse to follow the themed parent surface.

## Affected spots

Each of these repaints the exact color its parent surface already provides in both stock light and dark:

- `.tiptap tr` rule in `src/app.css` (table rows in notes/editors)
- Edit User Group modal → Users tab body rows (`src/lib/components/admin/Users/Groups/Users.svelte`, common Modal surface)
- `selectClass` dark repaint in `AddToolServerModal.svelte`, `AddTerminalServerModal.svelte`, and `AddConnectionModal.svelte` - three copies of the same constant; the sibling input constant in the same files is already fully transparent
- Analytics Dashboard's inline "Model Usage" / "User Activity" row markup (`src/lib/components/admin/Analytics/Dashboard.svelte`, two rows)
- Evaluations Feedbacks + Leaderboard body rows (settings modal surface)
- admin UserList body rows (app page surface)
- Chat markdown tables (`src/lib/components/chat/Messages/Markdown/MarkdownTokens.svelte`): thead and body rows - this thead painted the page's own color, unlike the tiptap editor's table header, which uses an intentional gray-850 contrast band
- CitationsModal source rows (common Modal surface)

## Scoping rule (what is deliberately left alone)

Only exact parent-surface repaints qualify: removal must be visually identical in stock light AND dark. Surfaces with intentional contrast or function are untouched - e.g. the tiptap table header's gray-850 band, sticky control bars that mask rows scrolling beneath them, disabled-state opacity scrims, and card-style containers that read as a deliberate surface idiom.

## Related

The same repaints existed in `ModelUsage.svelte` / `UserUsage.svelte`, but that is moot: those components were dead code and were removed in #27573 / #27574.

## Proposal

Remove the redundant repaints so these surfaces inherit their parent. No stock visual change; instance theming stops hitting opaque boxes. I have the change prepared and tested locally, and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: issue: two user profile hover previews can be open at once (Admin Users list) - same root cause as #27548
body:
## Bug Description

Two user profile hover previews can be open at the same time, one card stacked on the other - most visibly in the **Admin Panel → Users** list, where hovering one user's avatar and moving to a neighboring row can leave the previous user's profile card stuck open behind the new one.

This is the same root cause as #27548 (sidebar chat hover previews), which was fixed in #27549 - but for the *user profile* preview component, which was not covered by that fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Admin Panel → Users with several users in the list.
2. Hover a user's avatar until the profile preview card opens.
3. Move the pointer to the next row's avatar on a slightly diagonal path (drifting toward the preview card) and stop.
4. The new user's preview opens while the previous one remains stuck behind it.

## Expected Behavior

At most one profile preview is visible at any time; hovering (or clicking) a new user replaces the previous preview.

## Actual Behavior

The previous preview can remain open, overlapped by the new one. Additionally - unique to this component - `ProfilePreview` uses `openDelay={0}` with `closeDelay={200}`, so even ordinary row-to-row hovering can transiently show two stacked cards for up to 200 ms (the new card opens instantly while the old one's close timer is still pending).

## Root Cause

Identical to #27548: each `ProfilePreview.svelte` instance owns an independent bits-ui `LinkPreview.Root`, so nothing enforces a single-open invariant, and bits-ui's `SafePolygon` close path only re-evaluates on `pointermove` - a pointer that stops on a neighboring row while still inside the previous row's grace wedge leaves that preview open indefinitely. See #27548 for the full bits-ui trace.

`ProfilePreview` is shared by the Admin Users list, channel message avatars, the channel info member list, and the workspace member selector, so all four surfaces are affected and all four are covered by fixing the one component.

## Proposed Fix

Apply the same app-level invariant that #27549 added to `ChatItem.svelte`, in `ProfilePreview.svelte`: a module-context variable holds the close callback of the currently open preview; whenever any instance's preview opens (hover or click-toggle - both flow through the bound `open` state), it force-closes the previously registered one and registers itself. This also removes the 200 ms transient stack, since the old card is force-closed the instant the new one opens.

Out of scope, noted for transparency: `MentionToken.svelte` (@mention previews inside message prose) owns a separate *uncontrolled* `LinkPreview.Root` (no `bind:open`), which cannot join a force-close registry without restructuring; its inline-text geometry does not produce the stacked-rows failure reported here.

A PR with this fix will be linked shortly.

title: issue: connections without access grants lock out admins when BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL=false (Open Terminal icon never appears)
body:
## Bug Description

`has_connection_access` (`backend/open_webui/utils/access_control/__init__.py`) violates its own documented contract when `BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL=false`: a connection with missing/empty `access_grants` becomes inaccessible to **everyone - including the admins who configured it**.

The docstring says:

> - Admin with BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL → always allowed
> - Missing, None, or empty access_grants → private, **admin-only**
> - access_grants has entries → delegates to `has_access`

But the code only grants admins access through the bypass fast-path. With the bypass disabled, admins fall through to `has_access(user.id, 'read', [], ...)`, which returns `False` unconditionally for empty grants. There is no admin-only behavior anywhere.

## User-visible impact

On an instance running `BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL=false` (a deliberate hardening choice), an admin who adds an Open Terminal connection in **Admin → Settings → Integrations** never sees the terminal cloud icon in the chat input: `GET /api/v1/terminals/` filters the healthy, enabled connection out of the listing because a freshly created connection has `"access_grants": []`. The connection tests fine from the admin panel, making the missing icon look like a frontend bug. (Reproduced against a live instance; the same instance shows the icon immediately once the admin passes the access check.)

Since `has_connection_access` also guards external tool servers, MCP servers, and OpenAI connections, the same lockout applies to any of those configured without explicit grants under the hardened flag.

The Integrations UI compounds the confusion: the Open Terminal section states "All users will have access to file browsing and terminal tools through these servers," which is not true - access is grant-controlled, and a fresh connection has no grants at all.

Note: #27064 reports the same missing-icon symptom but is a **different bug** - that report's own diagnostics show `GET /api/v1/terminals/` returning the connection (the backend listing passes there; the failure is frontend-side on v0.10.2), whereas the defect reported here is precisely that the listing comes back empty. The fix below does not address #27064.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL=false`.
2. As an admin, add an Open Terminal connection under Admin → Settings → Integrations (leave access at its default - no grants).
3. Open a chat: the terminal cloud icon never appears, and `GET /api/v1/terminals/` returns `[]` even for the admin.
4. Unset the env var (default `true`): the icon appears - listing and access were the only difference; the connection was healthy throughout.

## Expected Behavior

Per the documented contract, a connection without grants is private to admins: admins can always see and use connections that only they can configure, regardless of the global bypass flag. Non-admin users require explicit grants either way.

## Proposed Fix

Implement the documented admin-only branch for the empty-grants case:

```diff
     if user.role == 'admin' and BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL:
         return True
 
+    access_grants = (connection.get('config') or {}).get('access_grants', [])
+    if not access_grants:
+        # No grants configured → private, admin-only: admins must keep access
+        # to connections only they can configure, even when they do not bypass
+        # access control globally.
+        return user.role == 'admin'
+
     if user_group_ids is None:
         user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id)}
 
-    access_grants = (connection.get('config') or {}).get('access_grants', [])
     return await has_access(user.id, 'read', access_grants, user_group_ids)
```

The change is strictly additive: admins gain access to ungranted connections when the bypass is off; no non-admin gains or loses anything; connections with grants resolve exactly as before. Moving the empty check above the group lookup also avoids a needless DB query for the common private case.

Additionally, correct the Integrations UI copy to reflect grant-controlled access.

A PR with this fix will be linked shortly.

## Environment

- **Open WebUI Version:** current `dev` branch (also reproduced on the current `:dev` Docker image, v0.11.0)
- **Deployment:** Docker, PostgreSQL

title: issue: model icons with transparent backgrounds get a white backdrop in the admin Models list, unlike workspace and model selector
body:
## Bug Description

Model profile images with transparent backgrounds (SVG logos, transparent PNGs) render with a hardcoded **white box behind them in the admin panel's Models list**, while the same images render transparently on the workspace Models page and in the chat input's model selector. The mismatch is most glaring in dark mode.

Credit to @Classic298 for spotting this; reproduced and confirmed independently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have models whose profile images are transparent-background SVGs/PNGs (e.g., provider logos).
2. Open Admin Panel → Settings → Models: each icon sits on a white rounded box.
3. Compare Workspace → Models and the chat input model selector: the same icons render with no backdrop.

## Expected Behavior

Model icons render consistently across all three surfaces - transparent images stay transparent, as they already do on the workspace page and in the model selector.

## Actual Behavior

Only the admin Models list forces a white backdrop, in both light and dark themes.

## Root Cause

The admin list's icon wrapper in `src/lib/components/admin/Settings/Models.svelte` is `<div class="flex bg-white rounded-xl">` - a hardcoded `bg-white` with no `dark:` variant, introduced in a July refactor (`43e792a8f`). The inner wrapper is even `bg-transparent`, so the white box shows through any transparent image. The workspace Models page wraps the identical image endpoint in a plain `bg-transparent` container, and the model selector applies no backdrop either.

## Proposed Fix

Remove the `bg-white` token from the wrapper (layout classes stay), restoring parity with the other two surfaces. One-token change; the file's remaining `bg-white` occurrences are hover-state utilities and the primary button, all correctly dark-paired.

title: issue: settings modal height stops scaling at 54rem, wasting vertical space and forcing scroll on large displays
body:
## Bug Description

The settings modal's height stops scaling at 54rem (864px). On tall displays (1440p, 4K, large ultrawides) the modal stays 864px tall while large amounts of vertical screen space sit unused above and below it - and settings tabs still require internal scrolling despite the free room.

Credit to @Classic298 for the report, originating from a user on a 38" ultrawide; reproduced and confirmed independently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a display taller than ~1080px (or devtools responsive mode at 2560×1440 / 3840×1600), open Settings (user or admin - same modal).
2. Open a long tab such as Admin → General.
3. The modal is capped at 864px tall; the tab content scrolls internally while the viewport has hundreds of unused vertical pixels.

## Expected Behavior

The modal's height keeps scaling proportionally with the viewport, the way its width already scales up to its cap.

## Actual Behavior

Height is hard-capped at `54rem` regardless of viewport size: `h-[min(54rem,calc(100dvh-4rem))]` in `src/lib/components/chat/SettingsModal.svelte`.

## Proposed Fix

Let the height cap scale on tall viewports while keeping today's behavior everywhere else:

```diff
-h-[min(54rem,calc(100dvh-4rem))] max-h-[calc(100dvh-4rem)]
+h-[min(max(54rem,80dvh),calc(100dvh-4rem))] max-h-[calc(100dvh-4rem)]
```

- Viewports ≤ ~1080px tall: `max(54rem, 80dvh)` resolves to 54rem - behavior byte-identical to today.
- Taller viewports: the modal grows to 80% of viewport height (864px → ~1152px at 1440p, ~1280px at 1600px), clamped by the existing `100dvh-4rem` guard.

The `max-w-[80rem]` width cap is deliberately left unchanged - settings rows stretched across an ultrawide would hurt readability; the wasted-space complaint is resolved by the vertical scaling.

A PR will be linked shortly.

### Expected Behavior

Saving a change to an older message in a chat updates that message. Which branch is current does not change, and the conversation renders in full after a reload.

### Actual Behavior

The chat renders truncated at that older message after a reload. Everything below it is off the current branch and no longer shown.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh Open WebUI v0.11.0 container with a clean DB, connected to any provider.
2. Admin Panel → Functions → `+` → Filter. Paste:

```python
class Filter:
    def outlet(self, body: dict, __user__: dict = None) -> dict:
        # modify the earliest user message, i.e. anything but the last message
        for message in (body.get("messages") or [])[:-1]:
            if message.get("role") == "user":
                message["content"] = (message.get("content") or "") + "."
                break
        return body
```

3. Save it, toggle it on, set it Global.
4. New chat, three turns, letting each answer finish.
5. `GET /api/v1/chats/<chat_id>`: `current_message_id` and `history.currentId` hold the id of the first user message, not the last assistant message.
6. Reload the page. The chat renders only the first user message.

The filter is only a minimal way to make an outlet write to an ancestor. Any writer that saves to a message other than the leaf produces the same result.

### Logs & Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Information

`ChatTable.upsert_message_to_history` (`models/chats.py:878`) ends with `history['currentId'] = message_id` outside every conditional, so any write to a message makes it the branch tip. In this repro the write comes from `outlet_filter_handler` (`utils/middleware.py:3549`), which persists `{content, originalContent}` for every message an outlet filter changed after the assistant message is already saved.

Fix, advancing the pointer only when the target is new or is a descendant of the current one:

```python
    messages = history.setdefault('messages', {})
    is_new = message_id not in messages

    ...

    current_id = history.get('currentId')
    if is_new or current_id not in messages:
        history['currentId'] = message_id
    else:
        node = message_id
        seen = set()
        while node and node not in seen:
            if node == current_id:
                history['currentId'] = message_id
                break
            seen.add(node)
            node = (messages.get(node) or {}).get('parentId')
```

A new message has to advance unconditionally: a regenerated answer and an edited prompt are siblings of the current leaf, not descendants, so a descendant-only test would store them and never show them.

title: issue: MCP tool OAuth redirect still drops the other enabled tools, skills, filters and feature toggles, and returns to / instead of the originating chat
body:
### Bug Report

**Discussion for approach alignment:** #27623
**Prior related issue (closed):** #18271
**Also related:** #25735 (model reset), #25812 / #22995 (closed unmerged)

### Description

When enabling an MCP tool that requires OAuth, the full-page OAuth redirect discards almost all chat state. The callback always returns the user to the site root (`/`), and on return only the single pending tool id is restored.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set a default model (e.g. `model-A`).
2. Create two MCP tools that require OAuth.
3. Open a **new chat** and manually switch the model to a non-default one (e.g. `model-B`).
4. Enable one of the MCP tools → you are redirected to the OAuth provider.
5. Complete the OAuth flow → you are redirected back to `/`.

### Expected Behavior

After the OAuth round-trip, the chat should retain:
- the originating chat route (`/c/{id}`)
- the selected model (`model-B`)
- the tool that just completed OAuth (enabled)
- other enabled tools, selected skills, filters
- feature toggles (web search / image generation / code interpreter)
- draft prompt text

### Actual Behavior

- The model falls back to the **default** (`model-A`), not the manually selected `model-B`.
- The OAuth'd tool is **not** enabled.
- Draft prompt, other tools/skills/filters, and toggles are lost.
- The user lands on `/` instead of the original chat.

### Root Cause (analysis)

In a new chat, the reactive that mirrors the model to `sessionStorage.selectedModels` is gated to existing chats only, so a manually picked model is never persisted before the manual-enable redirect. After the redirect the model falls back to default; that reassignment triggers the model-change reactive, which calls `resetInput()` and wipes even the restored tool selection.

The default-tool auto-flow path (`continueOAuthRedirect`) happens to work because it calls `saveSessionSelectedModels()` before redirecting.

### Environment

- Version: `dev` (reproduced on main @ ecd48e2f)
- Browser: any
- Deployment: Docker

### Notes

I have a working, tested front-end-only fix and have opened Discussion #27623 to align on the approach before submitting a PR.

title: issue: Enter in confirmation dialogs activates Cancel instead of confirming (v0.11.0 and dev)
body:
### Affected Version

`dev` (regression introduced after v0.11.0, by the interaction described below - not present in v0.11.0)

### Expected Behavior

Pressing Enter while a confirmation dialog is open (delete chat, delete message, delete folder/model/knowledge, etc.) confirms the action, as it always has.

### Actual Behavior

Pressing Enter closes the dialog **without** performing the action. Nothing is deleted; the dialog silently cancels.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On current `dev`, delete any chat from the sidebar (or delete one of your own messages in a chat).
2. When the confirmation dialog appears, press Enter.
3. The dialog closes and the chat/message is still there.

### Root Cause

#27491 correctly changed `ConfirmDialog`'s window-level Enter handler to defer to the focused control (`target.closest('a, button, textarea')` → let native activation happen). That fix's stated behavior - "Enter anywhere else still confirms as before" - is defeated by where focus actually lands: the dialog's focus trap is created with **no `initialFocus`**, so focus-trap falls back to the first tabbable node in the container, which is the **Cancel** button (as #27491's own description documents). The dialog therefore opens with Cancel invisibly focused, and Enter now natively activates Cancel.

The underlying defect is that `ConfirmDialog` never deliberately chose its initial focus - it never mattered while the old handler hijacked Enter globally, and #27491 (correctly) made focus meaningful, exposing the accidental Cancel default.

### Proposed Fix

Give the focus trap an explicit `initialFocus`: any input inside the dialog first (so typing dialogs still focus their field immediately), otherwise the **Confirm** button. This restores Enter-to-confirm with a *visible* focus ring on Confirm - preserving everything #27491 fixed (the focused control's label always matches what Enter does; Tab → Cancel → Enter cancels; Enter in the textarea inserts a newline).

Fix is implemented and manually verified; PR follows immediately.

title: feat: Render Open Terminal output files as downloadable attachments in chat
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions and found none comparable to my request.

### Verify Feature Scope

- [x] I believe this feature request is appropriately scoped for the Issues section as described above.

### Problem Description

When a model creates a file through the official Open Terminal integration, the file is successfully written and immediately becomes available in the Open Terminal file navigator.

The file navigator can:

- locate the file;
- preview supported formats;
- download the file using its existing authenticated download action.

However, the generated file is not rendered as a downloadable attachment inside the assistant message.

The model may instead return a Markdown link based on the local filesystem path, for example:

```text
/home/user/teste-terminal.xlsx
```

The browser resolves this relative path against the Open WebUI domain:

```text
https://<open-webui-domain>/home/user/teste-terminal.xlsx
```

This returns `404 Not Found` because `/home/user/...` is an Open Terminal filesystem path, not a public Open WebUI route.

The user is then required to:

1. open the Open Terminal sidebar;
2. navigate to the correct directory;
3. locate the generated file;
4. select it;
5. use the download button in the file navigator.

This is especially confusing because the assistant explicitly states that the file is available for download and displays a clickable link, but that link does not work.

The file itself is valid. Only its delivery inside the chat is missing.

### Proposed Solution

When an Open Terminal tool creates, writes, or displays a file, Open WebUI should be able to render that file as a downloadable attachment inside the assistant message.

For example:

```text
📎 teste-terminal.xlsx

[Preview] [Download]
```

The preferred implementation would reuse the same authenticated download action already used by the Open Terminal file navigator.

A possible flow would be:

1. An Open Terminal tool such as `display_file`, `write_file`, or a command execution result identifies an output file.

2. The tool result includes structured file metadata, for example:

```json
{
  "type": "terminal_file",
  "terminal_id": "<terminal-connection-id>",
  "path": "/home/user/teste-terminal.xlsx",
  "name": "teste-terminal.xlsx",
  "content_type": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
}
```

3. Open WebUI stores this metadata as part of the tool result or assistant message.

4. The chat frontend renders a file attachment component instead of relying on the model to construct a Markdown URL.

5. Clicking `Download` invokes the existing authenticated Open Terminal download handler used by the file navigator.

6. Clicking `Preview` may reuse the existing file preview component when the file type is supported.

The download must continue to respect:

- the current authenticated user;
- access to the selected Open Terminal connection;
- any Open Terminal multi-user filesystem restrictions;
- the configured file-browser root;
- disabled or unavailable terminal connections.

The local filesystem path should never need to become publicly accessible.

#### Optional explicit tool behavior

`display_file` could optionally support a parameter such as:

```text
attach_to_chat=true
```

This would allow the model or tool implementation to explicitly indicate that the displayed file should also appear as a chat attachment.

Open WebUI could also automatically apply this behavior when a tool result identifies a newly created file.

#### Alternative backend delivery

If reusing the Open Terminal download action is not practical, Open WebUI could copy or register the terminal file in its own file storage and return an authenticated file endpoint.

For installations using S3-compatible storage, another possible fallback would be a short-lived signed download URL.

These alternatives should remain implementation details. From the user's perspective, the result should simply be a downloadable file attachment in the chat.


### Alternatives Considered

#### Use the Open Terminal file navigator manually

The existing file navigator works correctly, but requiring users to manually locate every generated output adds unnecessary steps.

The assistant already knows which file was created, and Open WebUI already knows which terminal connection and filesystem path were involved.

#### Instruct the model not to create Markdown links

A system prompt can tell the model not to convert local paths into links and instead instruct the user to use the sidebar.

This prevents the invalid `404` link, but it does not provide a direct download experience.

#### Publish the Open Terminal home directory through NGINX

A directory such as `/home/user/downloads` could be exposed as `/downloads/`.

This would create working links, but introduces security and operational problems:

- terminal files may become publicly accessible;
- authorization would be separate from Open WebUI;
- filenames would need to be unpredictable;
- files would require automatic expiration and cleanup;
- multi-user isolation would be difficult;
- internal filesystem paths would become coupled to public URLs.

#### Upload every generated file to S3 or MinIO

A separate publishing service could upload terminal outputs and return signed URLs.

This is technically possible, but requires:

- additional credentials;
- custom publishing logic;
- object lifecycle rules;
- temporary URL management;
- user ownership handling;
- synchronization between Open Terminal and external storage.

This should not be required when Open WebUI already has an authenticated download action for the same file.

#### Register the file through the Open WebUI Files API

The terminal output could be copied into Open WebUI file storage.

This is a valid implementation alternative, but requires associating the uploaded file with the correct user and chat. Reusing the existing Open Terminal download mechanism appears simpler and avoids duplicating the file.


### Additional Context

Environment:

```text
Open WebUI: v0.11.0
Installation: Docker Compose
Open Terminal: configured through the official Open Terminal integration
Function calling: Native
Chat model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini through an OpenAI-compatible provider
Reverse proxy: NGINX
```

Reproduction steps:

1. Configure an Open Terminal connection in Open WebUI.

2. Enable Open Terminal tools for a model using Native function calling.

3. Ask the model:

```text
Create an XLSX file named teste-terminal.xlsx with the columns
Name, Department, and Status, containing five fictional records.
Make the file available for download.
```

4. The model successfully creates:

```text
/home/user/teste-terminal.xlsx
```

5. The Open Terminal file navigator refreshes and displays the file.

6. The XLSX preview works correctly.

7. The file navigator's download button downloads the file correctly.

8. The assistant response presents a Markdown link based on the local path.

9. Clicking the link opens:

```text
https://<open-webui-domain>/home/user/teste-terminal.xlsx
```

10. Open WebUI returns:

```text
404 Not Found
```

Expected result:

The assistant message should contain a downloadable attachment backed by the same authenticated action already available in the Open Terminal file navigator.

Related discussion:

```text
#14658
```

That discussion concerns generic generated-file links such as:

```text
sandbox:/mnt/data/file.pptx
```

This request is more narrowly scoped to the official Open Terminal integration, where Open WebUI already has:

- the terminal connection;
- the filesystem path;
- the authenticated user;
- the file preview;
- a working download action.

The requested feature is primarily to expose that existing capability directly inside the chat message.

title: feat: Web loader (fetch_url / RAG web) only supports Playwright server endpoints, not CDP - add a connection-mode switch
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions and found none comparable to my request.

### Verify Feature Scope

- [x] I believe this feature request is appropriately scoped for the Issues section as described above.

### Problem Description


  When `WEB_LOADER_ENGINE=playwright` with a remote browser set via `PLAYWRIGHT_WS_URL`, `SafePlaywrightURLLoader` connects
  using:

  ```python
  browser = p.chromium.connect(self.playwright_ws_url)        # lazy_load (sync)
  browser = await p.chromium.connect(self.playwright_ws_url)  # alazy_load (async)
  ```

  `chromium.connect()` only speaks Playwright's **server** protocol, so it does **not** work against a **CDP** endpoint - i.e.
  raw `chrome --remote-debugging`, `chromedp`, or a browserless/Chrome instance exposed as `ws://host?token=...`.

  Against a CDP endpoint the call hangs until timeout and throws inside `playwright/_impl/_json_pipe.py` (`KeyError: 'error'`),
  so every `fetch_url` / web-search page load fails. The **same URL** works with `p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(...)`, but there
  is no config option to select that - so anyone pointing at a CDP browser (a very common setup) must patch the source.

  **Confirmed on v0.11.0:** `connect()` times out; `connect_over_cdp()` connects and loads pages normally (`Browser.getVersion`
  → `HeadlessChrome/119...`).


### Proposed Solution

 Add a connection-protocol switch, defaulting to today's behavior so nothing changes for existing users.

  - **New setting:** `WEB_LOADER_PLAYWRIGHT_PROTOCOL` (env) / `web.loader.playwright_protocol` (config)
  - **Values:** `server` (default) · `cdp`

  Use it at both connect sites in `SafePlaywrightURLLoader`:

  ```python
  connect = (
      p.chromium.connect_over_cdp
      if self.playwright_protocol == "cdp"
      else p.chromium.connect
  )
  browser = connect(self.playwright_ws_url)   # add `await` in alazy_load
  ```

  This makes both Playwright-server and CDP remote browsers first-class with a one-line branch.

  > An auto-fallback to `connect_over_cdp()` when `connect()` fails the handshake would also work, but an explicit switch is
  simpler and more predictable.


### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

title: issue: no way to reset a model avatar to the default logo since the v0.11.0 model editor redesign
body:
### Affected Version

v0.11.0 / current `dev`

### Expected Behavior

The model editor offers a way to reset a model's avatar back to the default logo, as it did through v0.10.2 (the "Reset Image" button under the avatar).

### Actual Behavior

There is no way to reset a model's avatar anymore, in either the workspace model editor or the admin model editor (both render the same `ModelEditor` component). Clicking the avatar only opens the file picker, so once a model has a custom image it can only ever be replaced, never cleared.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Workspace → Models → edit any model (or Admin Panel → Settings → Models → edit).
2. Upload a custom avatar image and save.
3. Try to restore the default logo. The avatar button only opens the file picker; no reset control exists anywhere in the editor.

### Root Cause

The model editor redesign (commit `b92f59230`, first shipped in v0.11.0) dropped the "Reset Image" button and its `en-US` i18n key from `src/lib/components/workspace/Models/ModelEditor.svelte`. Through v0.10.2 the editor had:

```svelte
<button
	class="px-2 py-1 text-gray-500 rounded-lg text-xs"
	on:click={() => {
		info.meta.profile_image_url = `${WEBUI_BASE_URL}/static/favicon.png`;
	}}
	type="button"
>
	{$i18n.t('Reset Image')}</button
>
```

This looks like an unintended casualty of the visual overhaul rather than a deliberate removal - it re-opens exactly what #7278 originally reported.

### Additional Information

Notes for whoever restores it, from prototyping a fix (a restoration branch exists at `silentoplayz:fix/model-avatar-reset` and can become a PR once the preferred design is clear):

- Any design that shows the reset control **only when a custom image is set** has to classify "default", and the default currently has three representations depending on where the model came from: the editor's absolute `${WEBUI_BASE_URL}/static/favicon.png`, the backend's relative `/static/favicon.png` (`routers/models.py`), and an **absent key** - the editor's model-load does a shallow merge (`info = { ...info, ...model }`), so a model `meta` without `profile_image_url` replaces the default wholesale and the favicon you see is only the template's else-fallback. The original button avoided all of this by being unconditional (resetting an already-default model is a harmless no-op).
- The redesigned header is a full-width row (avatar beside the name/ID inputs), so the old `justify-end` placement no longer reads as "next to the avatar" on wide screens - the control probably wants to sit directly under or on the avatar in the new layout. Open to whatever placement fits the design direction.

title: issue: Open Terminal cloud icon and Account profile avatar are cut off on their left side
body:
### Check Existing Issues

Linux

Firefox

### Confirmation

- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.
- [x] I have included the Docker container logs.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup.**

### Expected Behavior

1. The Open Terminal cloud icon in the chat input renders fully rounded on its left side, in both its untoggled and toggled (server selected) states.
2. The profile avatar in **Settings → Account** renders as a complete circle with its ring fully visible.

### Actual Behavior

Two independent UI elements are visibly cut off on their left-hand side:

1. **Open Terminal cloud icon (chat input)** - the left bump of the cloud is shaved flat, in both the untoggled and toggled states.
2. **Account profile avatar (Settings → Account)** - the avatar circle's left edge is chopped flat. This is image-independent: it happens with an uploaded photo, the initials avatar, and the default profile image alike, and worsens on hover (the hover ring is 2px).

### Steps to Reproduce

**Cloud icon:**
1. Configure any terminal server (system or direct) so the Open Terminal selector appears in the chat input, with a terminal-capable model selected.
2. Look closely at the cloud icon next to the input - its left side is flattened. Select a terminal so the label appears; the clipping persists.

**Account avatar:**
1. Open **Settings → Account**.
2. Look at the round profile avatar under **Profile** - its left edge is cut flat. Hover it and the cut becomes more pronounced.

### Root Cause

Both bugs share one story - **artwork drawn flush against a clipping boundary gets its left edge shaved**, especially at fractional device-pixel positions:

1. **Cloud icon** (`src/lib/components/icons/Cloud.svelte`): the cloud path touches `x=1` and `x=23` in a 24-unit viewBox. The chat input renders it with `stroke-width="2"`, so the stroke's outer edge lands *exactly* on the viewBox boundary - where the SVG's default `overflow: hidden` clips it. No ancestor container is involved (verified by walking the computed styles of every ancestor: the icon sits 40+ px inside the nearest scroll container; the svg's own viewport is the only clipper).
2. **Account avatar** (`src/lib/components/chat/Settings/Account/UserProfileImage.svelte`, `variant="account"`): the avatar button sits *exactly* flush-left (measured: identical fractional `getBoundingClientRect().left` values) with two clipping ancestors - the tab's `overflow-y-auto` scroll wrapper and the settings modal's `overflow-hidden` content pane. Its `ring-1` / `hover:ring-2` is an **outset** box-shadow, so the ring plus the boundary pixel of the circle is clipped on the left. (`overflow-y-auto` forces `overflow-x` to compute to `auto`, so the horizontal clip applies even though only vertical scrolling was intended.)

### Proposed Fix

A one-class change per bug, PR to follow:

1. `Cloud.svelte`: add `overflow-visible` to the svg - zero geometry change; simply stops the SVG viewport from clipping its own legitimate artwork. All four Cloud usages benefit.
2. `UserProfileImage.svelte` (account variant): change the ring to `ring-inset` (existing precedent in `FileEntryRow.svelte`), so the ring draws inside the button bounds where nothing can clip it.

title: feat: Forward raw attachments as native provider file inputs
body:
### Check Existing Issues - [x] I have searched all existing **open AND closed** issues and discussions and found none comparable to my request. ### Verify Feature Scope - [x] I believe this feature request is appropriately scoped for the Issues section as described above. ### Problem Description Feature request: Forward raw attachments as native provider file inputs

Summary

PR #27627 introduces a valuable File Processing model capability that allows files to be uploaded with process=false, skipping extraction, OCR, chunking, embeddings, and RAG injection.

This solves the storage and preprocessing side of raw attachments. However, for direct provider connections, the raw file is still not forwarded to the model. When File Processing is disabled, Open WebUI stores the original file and retains its reference in metadata.files, but GPT, Claude, and other directly connected models cannot read its contents.

I propose adding a second, provider-aware capability that forwards raw attachments to APIs that support native file inputs.

Current behavior

With File Processing enabled:

File upload
→ extraction/OCR
→ chunking and optional embeddings
→ RAG or full-text context
→ extracted text sent to the model

With File Processing disabled by #27627:

File upload
→ process=false
→ original bytes stored
→ file excluded from RAG
→ file reference retained in metadata.files
→ pipe/backend may fetch and process the raw file

This works well for pipe-backed models, but direct provider connections currently stop at the file reference:

Raw attachment
→ stored by Open WebUI
→ not forwarded to the provider
→ direct model cannot inspect the document

Proposed capability

Add a model capability such as:

{
  "capabilities": {
    "file_upload": true,
    "file_processing": false,
    "native_file_input": true
  }
}

The capabilities would have distinct meanings:

  • file_upload: users may attach files.

  • file_processing: Open WebUI extracts and indexes file content.

  • native_file_input: Open WebUI forwards the original file to the provider in its native file-input format.

Suggested behavior:

File Processing | Native File Input | Behavior -- | -- | -- On | Any | Existing extraction and RAG behavior Off | Off | Raw attachment available only to pipes, tools, or external backends Off | On | Raw attachment forwarded directly to the provider

This avoids treating "skip extraction" and "send to the model" as the same capability.

Suggested implementation path

The infrastructure added by #27627 already provides most of the common foundation:

  • upload through the existing process=false path;

  • original bytes retained in Open WebUI storage;

  • processed: false stamped on the attachment;

  • raw files excluded from RAG and full-context retrieval;

  • file IDs retained in metadata.files;

  • existing storage and access-control mechanisms.

The remaining work could be implemented as a provider-specific attachment adapter in the backend.

Conceptually:

class NativeAttachmentAdapter:
    def supports(self, model, mime_type) -> bool:
        ...

    async def build_content_part(self, file, connection, user) -> dict:
        ...

Possible initial adapters:

OpenAI Responses API
Anthropic Messages API
Gemini native file inputs

The adapter should:

  1. Identify processed: false files in metadata.files.

  2. Verify that the selected model supports native_file_input.

  3. Revalidate user access to each file.

  4. Read the original bytes through Storage.get_file.

  5. Convert the file to the provider-specific request format.

  6. Append the native file part to the latest user message.

  7. Ensure the same file is not also injected through RAG.

OpenAI Responses API

For OpenAI direct connections configured with api_type: responses, a PDF could be converted to an input_file content part:

{
  "type": "input_file",
  "filename": "document.pdf",
  "file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,JVBERi0x..."
}

The existing convert_to_responses_payload already converts:

text → input_text
image_url → input_image

It could be extended to also convert an internal raw-file content part into input_file.

For an initial implementation, inline base64 would be sufficient. A later optimization could upload the file to the provider Files API and cache the provider file ID for reuse across turns.

Anthropic Messages API

For Anthropic-native connections, the equivalent PDF part would be:

{
  "type": "document",
  "source": {
    "type": "base64",
    "media_type": "application/pdf",
    "data": "JVBERi0x..."
  }
}

This would require the direct Anthropic chat path to use the native Messages API rather than only the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint.

Because that is a larger change, it may make sense to implement OpenAI Responses support first and treat Anthropic Messages as a follow-up adapter using the same attachment abstraction.

Base64 versus provider file IDs

The first version should probably use base64 because:

  • it does not require provider-side file lifecycle management;

  • it works without a separate Files API;

  • it is deterministic and easy to test;

  • the stored Open WebUI file remains the source of truth.

Provider file IDs could be added later as an optimization for large files and repeated multi-turn use.

A cached mapping might look like:

{
  "provider_files": {
    "openai:connection-0": {
      "file_id": "file_abc123",
      "file_hash": "...",
      "created_at": 1785310000
    }
  }
}

The file hash already stored by Open WebUI could be used to avoid duplicate provider uploads.

UX

The feature does not necessarily require a second upload button.

For dedicated native-document models, the model capabilities could determine the behavior automatically:

GPT Native Documents
Claude Native Documents
Gemini Native Files

When such a model is selected:

File Processing = off
Native File Input = on

Normal "Upload Files" would store and forward the original file.

A per-file selector could be considered later for mixed workflows such as:

PDF A → native provider input
PDF B → RAG
XLSX → external analysis tool

However, model-level behavior would be a smaller and more consistent first implementation, following the capability design introduced by #27627.

Important safeguards

The implementation should:

  • fail clearly when the provider or model does not support the MIME type;

  • never silently fall back from native input to extracted text;

  • enforce separate size and file-count limits for native attachments;

  • account for base64 expansion in request-size limits;

  • avoid duplicating the same document as both native input and RAG context;

  • revalidate access before reading file bytes;

  • define behavior for temporary chats;

  • preserve filenames and MIME types;

  • avoid storing base64 strings in the frontend or chat database.

Base64 conversion should happen in the backend immediately before the provider request.

Multi-turn behavior

For an MVP, the file could be resent in each request.

Longer term, provider Files APIs or stateful Responses API conversations could reduce repeated payload size. This should probably be treated as an optimization rather than a blocker for initial native PDF support.

The contract should be explicit:

  • either the native file remains available in subsequent turns;

  • or the UI indicates that the file only applies to the current request.

Silent loss of document context across turns should be avoided.

Scope suggestion

A contained first PR could support:

  • OpenAI direct connections only;

  • Responses API only;

  • PDF files only;

  • inline base64 only;

  • saved chats only;

  • model-level native_file_input capability;

  • no automatic provider Files API upload.

That would provide a useful end-to-end implementation without requiring an immediate provider-agnostic solution.

A later PR could add:

  • Anthropic Messages document blocks;

  • Gemini native files;

  • provider file-ID caching;

  • additional MIME types;

  • temporary-chat support;

  • per-file mode selection.

Why this matters

Modern providers can inspect PDFs natively, including page layout, images, diagrams, and tables. Open WebUI currently reduces these documents to extracted text before sending them to direct models.

The combination of #27627 and native provider forwarding would allow Open WebUI to support both workflows cleanly:

RAG-oriented models
→ extract and retrieve text

Native-document models
→ send the original file

Custom backends
→ receive raw file references and handle them independently

This would preserve the existing behavior by default while allowing capable providers to use their native document-understanding APIs.

Relationship to #27627

This proposal is intended as a follow-up to #27627, not a replacement.

#27627 solves:

Store raw files without Open WebUI processing

This feature would solve:

Forward those raw files to supported direct providers

Together, they would complete the raw-attachment path from the chat UI to the model.

title: issue: chat delete controls remain visible when the chat delete permission is disabled
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues.
- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions.
- [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items (your issue might already be addressed on the development branch!).
- [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI.

Closest prior art, both closed and neither covering this: #993 (2024 - the `Delete All Chats` control actually deleted chats without permission; the backend check was added, but the control was never hidden) and #25920 (`delete_folder_by_id` bypassing `chat.delete`, a backend fix).

### Installation Method

Git Clone

### Open WebUI Version

`dev` @ 810378c0b (v0.11.0)

### Operating System

Linux

### Browser (if applicable)

Firefox

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup** - the only setting that matters is the `chat.delete` user permission (`Allow Chat Delete`), reproducible on a default install with no environment variables set.
- [x] I have documented step-by-step reproduction instructions below.

> [!NOTE]
> Browser console logs and Docker container logs are not applicable here: this is a frontend conditional-rendering gap identified by reading the code, and the failing request returns a clean `401` with the expected `ACCESS_PROHIBITED` detail - there is no crash or stack trace to attach. A PR fixing it accompanies this issue.

### Expected Behavior

When an admin disables the `chat.delete` permission (`Allow Chat Delete`) for a user, the chat deletion controls should not be offered to that user - the same way disabling `chat.share`, `chat.export`, or `chat.import` already hides their respective controls.

### Actual Behavior

Every chat deletion control remains visible and clickable. Using any of them fails with `You do not have permission to access this resource. Please contact your administrator for assistance.` - a dead control that advertises a capability the user does not have.

Concretely, `chat.delete` is currently the **only** permission key that the backend enforces but the frontend never checks anywhere. The controls affected:

| # | Entry point | Location |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sidebar chat `⋯` menu → **Delete** | `Sidebar/ChatMenu.svelte` |
| 2 | Sidebar **Shift + hover** inline trash icon | `Sidebar/ChatItem.svelte` |
| 3 | Sidebar hidden keyboard-shortcut target (`#delete-chat-button`) | `Sidebar/ChatItem.svelte` |
| 4 | Open chat's top navbar `⋯` menu → **Delete** | `layout/Navbar/Menu.svelte` |
| 5 | Search modal chat `⋯` menu → **Delete** | via `ChatMenu.svelte` |
| 6 | Search modal **Shift-held** inline trash icon | `layout/SearchModal.svelte` |
| 7 | Settings → Data Controls → **Delete All Chats** | `chat/Settings/DataControls.svelte` |
| 8 | Settings → Archived Chats → per-row trash icon | `chat/Settings/ArchivedChats.svelte` |

The backend side is correct and needs no change - `chat.delete` is enforced for non-admins at:

- `DELETE /api/v1/chats/{id}` - `routers/chats.py`
- `DELETE /api/v1/chats/` (delete all) - `routers/chats.py`
- `DELETE /api/v1/folders/{id}` when the folder contains chats - `routers/folders.py`

The inconsistency is visible within single files: `DataControls.svelte` gates its **Import Chats** and **Export Chats** rows on `chat.import` / `chat.export`, but leaves **Delete All Chats** ungated three rows below. `ChatMenu.svelte` gates share, export, and clone, but not delete.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and launch Open WebUI on `dev` with default settings (no environment variables required).
2. Sign in as an **admin**.
3. Create a second, **non-admin** user, and sign in as that user in another browser/profile. Send one message so a chat exists in the sidebar, then archive a second chat so the Archived Chats list is non-empty.
4. As the **admin**, go to **Admin Panel → Users → Default Permissions → Chat** and turn **Allow Chat Delete** **off**. Save.
5. As the **non-admin** user, reload the page, then observe each control below is still rendered:
   - Hover a chat in the sidebar → click the `⋯` menu → **Delete** is present.
   - Hold **Shift** and hover a sidebar chat → an inline trash icon appears next to Archive.
   - Open a chat → click the `⋯` menu in the top navbar → **Delete** is present.
   - Open the Search modal → the per-result `⋯` menu shows **Delete**; holding **Shift** shows an inline trash icon.
   - **Settings → Data Controls** → the **Delete All Chats** row with its **Delete All** button is present (while **Import Chats** and **Export Chats** are correctly hidden if those permissions are off).
   - **Settings → Archived Chats** → each row shows a trash icon.
6. Click any of them and confirm the deletion dialog.

**Expected at step 6:** the control was never offered.
**Actual at step 6:** the request returns `401` and a toast reads `You do not have permission to access this resource. Please contact your administrator for assistance.` The chat is not deleted, so there is no data-loss risk - but the user is handed a control that can only ever fail.

### Additional Information

Suggested fix: apply the condition the backend already enforces (`$user?.role === 'admin' || ($user?.permissions?.chat?.delete ?? true)`) to the eight affordances above, matching the existing `chat.share` / `chat.export` / `chat.import` gates in the same components. This reuses the existing permission and adds no new setting or configuration surface.

Note that the folder-deletion path is deliberately **not** a candidate for hiding: `DELETE /api/v1/folders/{id}` only requires `chat.delete` *when the folder contains chats*, so a static gate would wrongly hide folder deletion for empty folders. Surfacing the error there is correct behavior.

This issue was prepared with AI copilot assistance and has been reviewed and manually tested by the author.

title: issue: public_tools and public_notes sharing permissions default to enabled in SharingPermissions, disagreeing with the config
body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related issues.
- [x] I have searched for any existing and/or related discussions.
- [x] I have also searched in the CLOSED issues AND CLOSED discussions and found no related items (your issue might already be addressed on the development branch!).
- [x] I am using the latest version of Open WebUI.

This is the same bug **class** as #27120 (fixed by #27296, merged) - the `SharingPermissions` model disagreeing with the config - but a different mechanism and different keys: #27120 was a *missing* field, this is two *present* fields whose defaults are inverted. No open or closed issue covers `public_tools` / `public_notes`.

### Installation Method

Git Clone

### Open WebUI Version

`dev` @ 810378c0b (v0.11.0)

### Operating System

Linux

### Browser (if applicable)

Not browser-dependent - the defect is in the backend model.

### Confirmation

- [x] I have read and followed all instructions in `README.md`.
- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have **provided every relevant configuration, setting, and environment variable used in my setup** - reproducible with no environment variables set; the relevant env defaults (`USER_PERMISSIONS_WORKSPACE_TOOLS_ALLOW_PUBLIC_SHARING`, `USER_PERMISSIONS_NOTES_ALLOW_PUBLIC_SHARING`) are both `False`.
- [x] I have documented step-by-step reproduction instructions below.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Precondition, stated up front:** this does **not** reproduce on a brand-new install. It requires the stored `user.permissions` config row to be missing the `sharing.public_tools` / `sharing.public_notes` keys - which is the case for any instance that saved default permissions **before those keys existed** and has since been upgraded (`public_tools` was added in `50b3f47f8`, 2025-03-31; `public_notes` in `41e4e7395`). It also reproduces on a current install for any client that `POST`s a permissions payload omitting those keys. Fresh installs are unaffected because a full payload is always written back.

> [!NOTE]
> Browser and container logs are not applicable: nothing errors or crashes. The failure mode is silently-wrong permission values. Evidence is an executable reproduction against the real model classes, below. A PR fixing it accompanies this issue.

### Expected Behavior

The `SharingPermissions` Pydantic model's field defaults should match the config defaults in `DEFAULT_USER_PERMISSIONS`, so that the admin panel displays - and the endpoint persists - the same value the permission enforcer actually applies.

### Actual Behavior

Two fields are inverted relative to their config defaults:

| `sharing` key | env default (`config.py`) | frontend `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS` | `SharingPermissions` (`routers/users.py`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public_models` | `False` | `false` | `False` ✅ |
| `public_knowledge` | `False` | `false` | `False` ✅ |
| `public_prompts` | `False` | `false` | `False` ✅ |
| **`public_tools`** | **`False`** | **`false`** | **`True`** ❌ |
| **`public_notes`** | **`False`** | **`false`** | **`True`** ❌ |

This looks like an incomplete normalization rather than an intentional choice: `50b3f47f8` originally introduced `public_models`/`public_knowledge`/`public_prompts`/`public_tools` all defaulting to `True`, and `f69e37a85` later corrected the first three to `False` to match the config - leaving `public_tools` (and, separately introduced, `public_notes`) behind.

**Why it matters - the read and enforce paths fill missing keys from different sources:**

- `GET /api/v1/users/default/permissions` builds `SharingPermissions(**user_permissions.get('sharing', {}))`, so a missing key is filled from the **model** default (`True`).
- `has_permission(...)` calls `fill_missing_permissions(default_permissions, DEFAULT_USER_PERMISSIONS)`, so the same missing key is filled from the **config** default (`False`).
- `Config.get('user.permissions')` returns the stored DB row **verbatim** - there is no merge or reseed on boot - so the gap persists indefinitely.

The result is a fail-open escalation, not merely a cosmetic mismatch. The admin panel loads the `GET` result and `POST`s the whole object back (`updateDefaultPermissionsHandler` in `admin/Users/Groups.svelte` passes `group.permissions` straight to `updateUserDefaultPermissions`), so **saving any unrelated permission toggle persists the phantom `True`** - granting every user public tool and note sharing that the admin never enabled.

Once persisted, it is enforced for real at six sites: `routers/tools.py` (×3) and `routers/notes.py` (×3), via `filter_allowed_access_grants(..., 'sharing.public_tools' | 'sharing.public_notes')`.

### Steps to Reproduce

**A. Deterministic reproduction of the model defect** (no instance required - run from `backend/`):

```python
from open_webui.routers.users import SharingPermissions, UserPermissions
from open_webui.config import DEFAULT_USER_PERMISSIONS as D
from open_webui.utils.access_control import fill_missing_permissions

# a stored config row that predates the two keys
stale = {k: v for k, v in D['sharing'].items() if k not in ('public_tools', 'public_notes')}
full = {g: dict(v) for g, v in D.items()}
full['sharing'] = stale

# 1. what GET /default/permissions returns (the admin panel's view)
got = {g: (SharingPermissions(**full[g]).model_dump() if g == 'sharing' else full[g]) for g in full}
# 2. what POST /default/permissions then writes back
posted = UserPermissions(**got).model_dump(by_alias=True)
# 3. what has_permission() actually enforces
enforced = fill_missing_permissions(dict(stale), D['sharing'])

for k in ('public_tools', 'public_notes'):
    print(k, 'GET:', got['sharing'][k], '| POST:', posted['sharing'][k], '| enforced:', enforced[k])
```

Output on current `dev`:

```
public_tools GET: True | POST: True | enforced: False
public_notes GET: True | POST: True | enforced: False
```

With the fix, all three columns read `False`.

**B. End-to-end on a live upgraded instance:**

1. Sign in as an admin and save default user permissions once, so a `user.permissions` config row exists.
2. Simulate the pre-existing row from an older version by removing the two keys (SQLite shown; adjust for Postgres):
   ```sql
   UPDATE config
      SET value = json_remove(value, '$.sharing.public_tools', '$.sharing.public_notes')
    WHERE key = 'user.permissions';
   ```
3. Open **Admin Panel → Users → Default Permissions → Sharing**.
   **Expected:** *Tools Public Sharing* and *Notes Public Sharing* show **off**, matching the env defaults.
   **Actual:** both show **on**, despite never having been enabled.
4. Toggle any unrelated permission and click **Save**, then re-check the DB row.
   **Expected:** the two keys are written as `false`.
   **Actual:** both are persisted as `true`, and non-admin users can now genuinely publish tools and notes publicly (the share dialog's public option sticks instead of being stripped by `filter_allowed_access_grants`).

### Additional Information

Suggested fix is a two-line change setting both model defaults to `False`, matching the config and the frontend template, and matching what `f69e37a85` already did for the sibling keys. No migration is needed: the correction only changes the value used when a key is *absent*, and an admin who genuinely wants public tool or note sharing still has the toggle.

For completeness, a full three-layer diff of all 65 permission keys (config `DEFAULT_USER_PERMISSIONS` ↔ the Pydantic models ↔ `src/lib/constants/permissions.ts`) shows these two are the only *default-value* divergences. The one remaining *missing-field* gap in the same model, `sharing.open_chats`, is already covered by #27607 / #27609, so the two changes are complementary and do not overlap.

This issue was prepared with AI copilot assistance; the reproduction above was executed against the real model classes on `dev` @ 810378c0b.

body:

### Confirmation

- [x] I am using the latest version of **both** Open WebUI and Ollama.
- [x] I have included the browser console logs.

- Specify exact install/launch/configure commands,
- List URLs visited, user input (incl. example values/emails/passwords if needed),
- Describe all options and toggles enabled or changed,
- Include any files or environmental changes,
- Identify the expected and actual result at each stage,
- Ensure any reasonably skilled user can follow and hit the same issue.


### Expected Behavior

Calling `search_calendar_events` with a `start` date but no `end` date should return events from that date forward, or an empty result set if none exist.

### Actual Behavior

PostgreSQL raises `psycopg.errors.NumericValueOutOfRange: bigint out of range`. The query parameter `end_ns` overflows PostgreSQL's `BIGINT` type (~9.22 × 10¹⁸ max) with a value of ~3.33 × 10¹⁹.

The tool returns a JSON error to the caller, making the tool unusable in the common case where a model asks "what's on my calendar for July 28?" without also specifying an end date.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy Open WebUI v0.11.0 with a **PostgreSQL** backend (SQLite is not affected; see Additional Information).
2. Authenticate as any user.
3. Tell the agent to use the `search_calendar_events` tool with only a `start` parameter. For example:
   ```
   start: "2026-07-28 00:00"
   ```
   (Do not provide an `end` parameter.)
4. Observe the error response instead of a valid (possibly empty) event list.

**Workaround:** Always provide an explicit `end` parameter when calling the tool (e.g. `end: "2026-08-28 00:00"`). The tool works correctly when both bounds are supplied.

### Root Cause

In `backend/open_webui/tools/builtin.py`, line 4012, the default `end_ns` computation for when no `end` is provided uses the constant `1_000_000_000_000`:

```python
else int(time.time() * 1_000) * 1_000_000 + 365 * 86400 * 1_000_000_000_000
```

1000 years into the future. That pushes the value to `3.15 × 10¹⁹ ns ≈ 1000 years`, which exceeds PostgreSQL BIGINT capacity by ~3.4×.


### Logs & Screenshots

**Error response from tool output:**

```
{
  "error": "(psycopg.errors.NumericValueOutOfRange) bigint out of range\n[SQL: SELECT calendar_event.id, calendar_event.calendar_id, calendar_event.user_id, calendar_event.title, calendar_event.description, calendar_event.start_at, calendar_event.end_at, calendar_event.all_day, calendar_event.rrule, calendar_event.color, calendar_event.location, calendar_event.data, calendar_event.meta, calendar_event.is_cancelled, calendar_event.created_at, calendar_event.updated_at, \"user\".id AS id_1, \"user\".email, \"user\".username, \"user\".role, \"user\".name, \"user\".profile_image_url, \"user\".profile_banner_image_url, \"user\".bio, \"user\".gender, \"user\".date_of_birth, \"user\".timezone, \"user\".presence_state, \"user\".status_emoji, \"user\".status_message, \"user\".status_expires_at, \"user\".info, \"user\".variables, \"user\".settings, \"user\".oauth, \"user\".scim, \"user\".last_active_at, \"user\".updated_at AS updated_at_1, \"user\".created_at AS created_at_1 \nFROM calendar_event LEFT OUTER JOIN \"user\" ON \"user\".id = calendar_event.user_id \nWHERE calendar_event.is_cancelled = false AND calendar_event.calendar_id IN (%(calendar_id_1_1)s::VARCHAR) AND (calendar_event.rrule IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at < %(start_at_1)s::BIGINT AND (calendar_event.end_at IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at >= %(start_at_2)s::BIGINT OR calendar_event.end_at IS NOT NULL AND calendar_event.end_at > %(end_at_1)s::BIGINT) OR calendar_event.rrule IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY calendar_event.start_at ASC]\n[parameters: {'start_at_1': 33321368250846000000, 'start_at_2': 1785211200000000000, 'end_at_1': 1785211200000000000, 'calendar_id_1_1': '4216c1e0-434a-4dfc-a213-65d3a9413838'}]\n(Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/9h9h)"
}
```

**Error in Docker container logs:**

```
2026-07-29 23:37:30.871 | ERROR    | open_webui.tools.builtin:search_calendar_events:4054 - search_calendar_events error: (psycopg.errors.NumericValueOutOfRange) bigint out of range
WHERE calendar_event.is_cancelled = false AND calendar_event.calendar_id IN (%(calendar_id_1_1)s::VARCHAR) AND (calendar_event.rrule IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at < %(start_at_1)s::BIGINT AND (calendar_event.end_at IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at >= %(start_at_2)s::BIGINT OR calendar_event.end_at IS NOT NULL AND calendar_event.end_at > %(end_at_1)s::BIGINT) OR calendar_event.rrule IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY calendar_event.start_at ASC]
psycopg.errors.NumericValueOutOfRange: bigint out of range
sqlalchemy.exc.DataError: (psycopg.errors.NumericValueOutOfRange) bigint out of range
WHERE calendar_event.is_cancelled = false AND calendar_event.calendar_id IN (%(calendar_id_1_1)s::VARCHAR) AND (calendar_event.rrule IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at < %(start_at_1)s::BIGINT AND (calendar_event.end_at IS NULL AND calendar_event.start_at >= %(start_at_2)s::BIGINT OR calendar_event.end_at IS NOT NULL AND calendar_event.end_at > %(end_at_1)s::BIGINT) OR calendar_event.rrule IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY calendar_event.start_at ASC]
```

No relevant error output in browser console.

### Additional Information

Occurs only when using PostgreSQL as a database backend. Does not occur with SQLite.

Open WebUI uses SQLite as its default database, which uses manifest typing. The `BIGINT` column declaration is advisory, not enforced. The overflow value of ~3.33 × 10¹⁹ is silently accepted and compared numerically against stored values without error. The bug is only visible when using PostgreSQL, which enforces `BIGINT` bounds at the protocol level. Any deployment using the default SQLite backend would never see this error, making it unlikely to surface during local development or testing.

**Scope:** The literal `1_000_000_000_000` appears exactly once in the entire codebase - only this line in `builtin.py:4012`. The `create_calendar_event` tool uses `3_600_000_000_000` (3600 × 10⁹ = 1 hour) as the default end time. No other code paths are affected.

## Setup

When adding an Open Terminal connection in Admin Panel → Settings → Integrations → Open Terminal and clicking Save, the request goes to POST /api/v1/users/user/settings/update instead of POST /api/v1/configs/terminal_servers. As a result, terminal_server.connections in the config table remains [] and the connection is never persisted. The AI cannot use the terminal because the backend lookup of the connection by ID always fails with "Terminal server not found".

Steps to reproduce:

Go to Admin Panel → Settings → Integrations → Open Terminal
Click + to add a new connection
